===== _commentary/v16/prompts/map3/surah_map.md (adapted) =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), an earlier reader's channel review (channels.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not delegate, browse or inspect files; run only the command the header describes.

The channel review is an earlier reader's proposal. Ignore its judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what it already assembled: start from its chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where its wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the surah,
and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear. A member
need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah, not in one
word. A chain may join a sense and its reversal as well as the parts of one scene. Mark a member attested only
inside a fixed expression [fixed expression]; add no other label to a member or a chain, and where a source
records a phrase and rejects it, say so of that phrase alone. When the dictionary itself joins two of the
surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at
the level of its objects, their parts and their operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into
another's more abstract function unless nothing concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test,
however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain; for
   each, name the speaker and the situation in a few words, and include the ayah that opens its scene when the
   passage continues one.
2. `## Interactions`. Where chains meet: a shared member, a dictionary phrase that joins members of two chains,
   a Quran passage that stages two chains together, or one chain's scene needing another's. One line each: the
   chains, where they meet, the evidence.
3. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: the chains its words take part in, what its words add to each, and in one
   line the whole scene each chain makes across the surah, so that a writer who sees only this ayah sees the
   scene, not a fragment.
4. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel you did not carry into a chain: one short line
   each, its name and why, no prose.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.

===== _commentary/v16/work/s027/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 27

- 27:1 طسٓ ۚ تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَكِتَابٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
- 27:2 هُدًۭى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 27:3 ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ
- 27:4 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
- 27:5 أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوٓءُ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرُونَ
- 27:6 وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى ٱلْقُرْءَانَ مِن لَّدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ
- 27:7 إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًۭا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍۢ قَبَسٍۢ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
- 27:8 فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 27:9 يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
- 27:10 وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّۭ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًۭا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ ۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
- 27:11 إِلَّا مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًۢا بَعْدَ سُوٓءٍۢ فَإِنِّى غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 27:12 وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍۢ ۖ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًۭا فَٰسِقِينَ
- 27:13 فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةًۭ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
- 27:14 وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًۭا وَعُلُوًّۭا ۚ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
- 27:15 وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ عِلْمًۭا ۖ وَقَالَا ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍۢ مِّنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 27:16 وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَٰنُ دَاوُۥدَ ۖ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَضْلُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
- 27:17 وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمَٰنَ جُنُودُهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
- 27:18 حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ وَادِ ٱلنَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌۭ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمْلُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مَسَٰكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
- 27:19 فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًۭا مِّن قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِى بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
- 27:20 وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيْرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِىَ لَآ أَرَى ٱلْهُدْهُدَ أَمْ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَآئِبِينَ
- 27:21 لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُۥ عَذَابًۭا شَدِيدًا أَوْ لَأَا۟ذْبَحَنَّهُۥٓ أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّى بِسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
- 27:22 فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍۢ فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍۭ بِنَبَإٍۢ يَقِينٍ
- 27:23 إِنِّى وَجَدتُّ ٱمْرَأَةًۭ تَمْلِكُهُمْ وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 27:24 وَجَدتُّهَا وَقَوْمَهَا يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
- 27:25 أَلَّا يَسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُخْفُونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ
- 27:26 ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ ۩
- 27:27 ۞ قَالَ سَنَنظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
- 27:28 ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَٰبِى هَٰذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ
- 27:29 قَالَتْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ إِنِّىٓ أُلْقِىَ إِلَىَّ كِتَٰبٌۭ كَرِيمٌ
- 27:30 إِنَّهُۥ مِن سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَإِنَّهُۥ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
- 27:31 أَلَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَىَّ وَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ
- 27:32 قَالَتْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَفْتُونِى فِىٓ أَمْرِى مَا كُنتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْرًا حَتَّىٰ تَشْهَدُونِ
- 27:33 قَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أُو۟لُوا۟ قُوَّةٍۢ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ وَٱلْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَٱنظُرِى مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ
- 27:34 قَالَتْ إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا۟ قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوٓا۟ أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَآ أَذِلَّةًۭ ۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
- 27:35 وَإِنِّى مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِم بِهَدِيَّةٍۢ فَنَاظِرَةٌۢ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
- 27:36 فَلَمَّا جَآءَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ قَالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍۢ فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم بَلْ أَنتُم بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ
- 27:37 ٱرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُم بِجُنُودٍۢ لَّا قِبَلَ لَهُم بِهَا وَلَنُخْرِجَنَّهُم مِّنْهَآ أَذِلَّةًۭ وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ
- 27:38 قَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِى بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ
- 27:39 قَالَ عِفْرِيتٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ ۖ وَإِنِّى عَلَيْهِ لَقَوِىٌّ أَمِينٌۭ
- 27:40 قَالَ ٱلَّذِى عِندَهُۥ عِلْمٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِندَهُۥ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّى لِيَبْلُوَنِىٓ ءَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ ۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّى غَنِىٌّۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
- 27:41 قَالَ نَكِّرُوا۟ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا نَنظُرْ أَتَهْتَدِىٓ أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
- 27:42 فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ قِيلَ أَهَٰكَذَا عَرْشُكِ ۖ قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ ۚ وَأُوتِينَا ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ
- 27:43 وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍۢ كَٰفِرِينَ
- 27:44 قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدْخُلِى ٱلصَّرْحَ ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةًۭ وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ صَرْحٌۭ مُّمَرَّدٌۭ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ ۗ قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 27:45 وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَٰلِحًا أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
- 27:46 قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ ۖ لَوْلَا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
- 27:47 قَالُوا۟ ٱطَّيَّرْنَا بِكَ وَبِمَن مَّعَكَ ۚ قَالَ طَٰٓئِرُكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ تُفْتَنُونَ
- 27:48 وَكَانَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍۢ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
- 27:49 قَالُوا۟ تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُۥ وَأَهْلَهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِۦ مَا شَهِدْنَا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
- 27:50 وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًۭا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًۭا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
- 27:51 فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَٰهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
- 27:52 فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةًۢ بِمَا ظَلَمُوٓا۟ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْلَمُونَ
- 27:53 وَأَنجَيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
- 27:54 وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
- 27:55 أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةًۭ مِّن دُونِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ تَجْهَلُونَ
- 27:56 ۞ فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍۢ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌۭ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ
- 27:57 فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
- 27:58 وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
- 27:59 قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰٓ ۗ ءَآللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
- 27:60 أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَنۢبَتْنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍۢ مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنۢبِتُوا۟ شَجَرَهَآ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌۭ يَعْدِلُونَ
- 27:61 أَمَّن جَعَلَ ٱلْأَرْضَ قَرَارًۭا وَجَعَلَ خِلَٰلَهَآ أَنْهَٰرًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
- 27:62 أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
- 27:63 أَمَّن يَهْدِيكُمْ فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَمَن يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦٓ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ تَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
- 27:64 أَمَّن يَبْدَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَمَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
- 27:65 قُل لَّا يَعْلَمُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ۚ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ
- 27:66 بَلِ ٱدَّٰرَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّنْهَا ۖ بَلْ هُم مِّنْهَا عَمُونَ
- 27:67 وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًۭا وَءَابَآؤُنَآ أَئِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ
- 27:68 لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا هَٰذَا نَحْنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبْلُ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 27:69 قُلْ سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
- 27:70 وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُن فِى ضَيْقٍۢ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
- 27:71 وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
- 27:72 قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
- 27:73 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ
- 27:74 وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
- 27:75 وَمَا مِنْ غَآئِبَةٍۢ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
- 27:76 إِنَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ يَقُصُّ عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَكْثَرَ ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ
- 27:77 وَإِنَّهُۥ لَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةٌۭ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 27:78 إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِى بَيْنَهُم بِحُكْمِهِۦ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
- 27:79 فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَى ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلْمُبِينِ
- 27:80 إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
- 27:81 وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَٰدِى ٱلْعُمْىِ عَن ضَلَٰلَتِهِمْ ۖ إِن تُسْمِعُ إِلَّا مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُم مُّسْلِمُونَ
- 27:82 ۞ وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَآبَّةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ كَانُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا لَا يُوقِنُونَ
- 27:83 وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ فَوْجًۭا مِّمَّن يُكَذِّبُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
- 27:84 حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُو قَالَ أَكَذَّبْتُم بِـَٔايَٰتِى وَلَمْ تُحِيطُوا۟ بِهَا عِلْمًا أَمَّاذَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
- 27:85 وَوَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِم بِمَا ظَلَمُوا۟ فَهُمْ لَا يَنطِقُونَ
- 27:86 أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا۟ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 27:87 وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ۚ وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَٰخِرِينَ
- 27:88 وَتَرَى ٱلْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةًۭ وَهِىَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِ ۚ صُنْعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَفْعَلُونَ
- 27:89 مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهَا وَهُم مِّن فَزَعٍۢ يَوْمَئِذٍ ءَامِنُونَ
- 27:90 وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِى ٱلنَّارِ هَلْ تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
- 27:91 إِنَّمَآ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ رَبَّ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْبَلْدَةِ ٱلَّذِى حَرَّمَهَا وَلَهُۥ كُلُّ شَىْءٍۢ ۖ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
- 27:92 وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَا۟ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ ۖ فَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَقُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ
- 27:93 وَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا ۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ

# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this
exact word. **Echo roots** are observed but withheld mappings: sound-family candidates, not identity.

## ء ي ي (root_000074): 27:1 ءَايَٰتُ, 27:12 ءَايَٰتٍ, 27:13 ءَايَٰتُنَا, 27:52 لَءَايَةً, 27:81 بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا, 27:82 بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا, 27:83 بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا, 27:84 بِـَٔايَٰتِى, 27:86 لَءَايَٰتٍ, 27:93 ءَايَٰتِهِۦ

- **B001** bekleyerek oyalanma — durup oyalanmak · isin imkanini beklemek · kalinacak veya oyalanilacak yer
  تأيا يتأيا تأييا أي تمكث؛ تأييت الأمر انتظرت إمكانه؛ ليست هذه بدار تئية أي مقام (maqayis)؛ تأيا أي توقف وتمكث؛ منزل تئية أي منزل تلبث وتحبس (sihah)
- **B002** kisiyi bilerek hedefleme — onu belirtisiyle bilerek kastetmek
  تآييت وأصله تعمدت آيته وشخصه (maqayis)؛ تآييته وتأييته إذا قصدت آيته وتعمدته (sihah)
- **B003** gorunen belirti — gorunen isaret · belirlenmis isaret · kisinin sahsi · topluca cikmak · kitaptaki harf toplulugu parcasi · gunesin isigi · gunesin isigi
  الآية العلامة؛ آية الرجل شخصه؛ خرج القوم بآيتهم أي بجماعتهم؛ آية القرآن لأنها جماعة حروف؛ إياة الشمس ضوءها لأنه كالعلامة لها (maqayis)؛ الآية العلامة والآية من آيات الله والجميع الآي (ayn)؛ الآية العلامة؛ آية الرجل شخصه؛ خرج القوم بآيتهم أي بجماعتهم؛ الآية من كتاب الله جماعة حروف؛ أياة الشمس ضوؤها (sihah)
- **B004** hangi belirleyicisi — soru, sart veya ilgiyle belirleyen ad · hangi olursa veya herhangi bir
  لم يجىء إلا في قولهم أي في الاستفهام (jamhara)؛ أي مثقلة بمنزلة من وما؛ أيهم أخوك؛ أيما الأخوين؛ أيا ما تحب؛ أي لا تنون لأن أي مضاف (ayn)؛ أي اسم معرب يستفهم به ويجازى؛ وقد يكون بمنزلة الذي؛ وقد يكون نعتا للنكرة؛ وأي قد يتعجب بها (sihah)
- **B005** nesne zamiri dayanagi — nesne zamiri icin dayanak unsur
  إياك ضربت فتكون إيا عمادا للكاف؛ ولا تكون إيا مع كاف ولا هاء ولا ياء في موضع الرفع والجر؛ إياك وزيدا (ayn)
- **B006** zaman sorusu — ne zaman anlaminda zaman sorusu
  أيان بمنزلة متى؛ يختلف في نونها فيقال هي أصلية ويقال هي زائدة (ayn)
- **B007** nice cok — ne kadar cok anlaminda nicelik birimi · ne kadar cok anlaminda varyant
  كأين في معنى كم؛ أصل بنائها أي (ayn)؛ تدخل على أي الكاف فينقل إلى تكثير العدد بمعنى كم؛ كائن وكأين (sihah)
- **B008** ey seslenmesi — yakin muhataba seslenme birimi · yakin veya uzak muhataba seslenme birimi · uzatilmis seslenme bicimi
  في النداء أي فلان وقد يمد آي فلان (ayn)؛ أيا من حروف النداء ينادى بها القريب والبعيد؛ أي حرف ينادى به القريب (sihah)
- **B009** yani aciklayicisi — anlami aciklayan yani birimi
  أي تفسيرا للمعاني أي كذا وكذا (ayn)؛ أي كلمة تتقدم التفسير تقول أي كذا بمعنى تريد كذا (sihah)
- **B010** yemin oncesi evet — yemin oncesi evet veya bilakis sozu

- **B005** dalgınlığından yararlanarak kandırma — dalgınlığından yararlanıp kandırmak · onun dalgınlığını fırsat bilmek
  التغفل ختل عن غفلة (ayn)؛ تغافلت عنه وتغفلته إذا اهتبلت غفلته (sihah)
- **B006** ayırt edici izi bulunmama — yön belirtisi ve bayındırlık izi bulunmayan arazi · damgasız hayvan · damgasız dişi deve · yön belirtisi olmayan yol · işaretsiz, uzak ve ıssız düzlük · işlenmemiş ölü araziler
  لكل ما لا معلم له غفل، أرض غفل لا علم بها، وناقة غفل لا سمة عليها (maqayis)؛ الغفل سبسب متيه بعيد لا علامة فيها، وطريق غفل لا علامة فيه، ودابة غفل لا سمة عليها (ayn)؛ الأغفال الموات، أرض غفل لا علم بها ولا أثر عمارة، أرض غفل لم تمطر، ودابة غفل لا سمة عليها (sihah)؛ أرض غفل لا منار بها (mufradat)
- **B007** deneyimsiz ya da kavrayışsız kimse — deneyimsiz veya değeri bilinmeyen adam · kavrayışı kıt kimse
  رجل غفل لم يجرب الأمور (maqayis;sihah)؛ المغفل من لا فطنة له، ورجل غفل ليس يعرف ما عنده، لا يعرف له حسب (ayn)؛ رجل غفل لم تسمه التجارب (mufradat)
- **B008** kendini göz önünden uzak tutma — kendisini insanlar arasında saklayıp adını duyurmamak
  غفل فلان نفسه أي كتمها في الناس ولم يشهرها (ayn)
- **B009** iyiliği de kötülüğü de beklenmeyen bağlı kimse — ne iyiliği umulan ne kötülüğünden korkulan bağlı kimse · bağlanıp etkisiz duruma gelmek
  الغفل المقيد لا يرجى خيره ولا يخشى شره وقد اغتفل والجميع الأغفال (ayn)
- **B010** alt dudak altındaki sakal tutamının iki yanı — alt dudak altındaki küçük sakal tutamının iki yanı
  والمغفلة التي في الحديث جانبا العنفقة (sihah)

# s027 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. P1 (27:1-14) - Disclosure Across Text, Flame, Body, and Conscience
- Semantic invariant: Something initially encoded, distant, enclosed, or inward becomes perceptible through a medium and demands a response.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:1-14 moves from the clear written/recited signs, through the fire and call, to the hand-sign and the inwardly certain but outwardly denied signs.
- Surprising reach: Disclosure is repeatedly materialized as a threshold event: letters are joined, a spark is taken from a fire, a hand exits a garment opening, and an inward assertion fails to cross into truthful speech.

#### Subchannel A. Joined letters become a received, clarifying recitation
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Written units are joined into a text, recited, received, and made to disclose knowledge as a visible sign.
- Active motifs: recitation and instruction (quranic:root_001210:B002/m01); written letter-sequence (quranic:root_001283:B002/m01); visible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01); meaning disclosed by speech, writing, or gesture (quranic:root_000170:B005/m01); received and learned speech (quranic:root_001372:B011/m01); knowledge opening to the knower (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:1,6 `ق ر ء` (قُرْءَان); 27:1 `ك ت ب` (كِتَاب); 27:1,12-13 `ء ي ي` (ءَايَات); 27:1,13 `ب ي ن` (مُبِين); 27:6 `ل ق ي` (تُلَقَّى); 27:6 `ع ل م` (عَلِيم).
- Synthesis: The text is not only an inscription but an ordered vocal event. Recitation carries joined written material into reception, while the sign and clarification motifs make that transfer an unveiling of meaning rather than a bare transmission of sounds.

#### Subchannel B. A distant fire becomes an ember, news, and a summons
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A traveler senses a remote fire, approaches for an ember or information, and instead encounters a raised call surrounded by abiding blessing.
- Active motifs: sensing by sight or hearing (quranic:root_000059:B002/m01); burning fire (quranic:root_001564:B002/m01); blazing flame (quranic:root_000821:B002/m01); ember taken from its source (quranic:root_001196:B001/m01); arrival (quranic:root_000009:B001/m01); news and inward knowledge (quranic:root_000387:B001/m01); raised call (quranic:root_001486:B002/m01); stable, growing blessing (quranic:root_000109:B004/m01); surrounding side or circuit (quranic:root_000373:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:7 `ء ن س` (ءَانَسْتُ), `ش ه ب` (شِهَاب), `ق ب س` (قَبَس), `ء ت ي` (ءَاتِيكُم), `خ ب ر` (خَبَر), and `ن و ر` (نَار); 27:8 `ن د و` (نُودِيَ), `ب ر ك` (بُورِكَ), `ح و ل` (حَوْلَهَا), and `ن و ر` (النَّار).
- Synthesis: The expected practical transaction, taking fire or obtaining news, is redirected into revelation. The same luminous center supplies heat, information, voice, and blessing, so approach to a material signal becomes entry into a communicative sacred perimeter.

#### Subchannel C. The enclosed hand exits as a visible, unblemished sign
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A hand enters a garment opening, crosses back outside, and appears white without bodily lesion.
- Active motifs: entry into an interior (quranic:root_000464:B001/m01); shirt opening (quranic:root_000283:B001/m01); bodily hand (quranic:root_001693:B001/m01); emergence from a containing state (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01); whiteness (quranic:root_000168:B001/m01); bodily blemish or leukoderma (quranic:root_000755:B003/m01); visible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:12 `د خ ل` (أَدْخِل), `ج ي ب` (جَيْبِكَ), `ي د ي` (يَدَكَ), `خ ر ج` (تَخْرُج), `ب ي ض` (بَيْضَاء), `س و ء` (سُوء), and `ء ي ي` (ءَايَات).
- Synthesis: The garment opening functions as a controlled threshold. What exits is visibly transformed, yet the lesion motif is explicitly cancelled, distinguishing a revelatory surface change from disease.

#### Subchannel D. Inward certainty is blocked from truthful outward speech
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Perception and inward certainty form, but denial, deceptive relabeling, and self-exalting speech prevent the recognized truth from being publicly affirmed.
- Active motifs: settled certainty (quranic:root_001696:B001/m01); mind and discrimination within the self (quranic:root_001533:B013/m01); insight of the heart (quranic:root_000121:B002/m01); denial of what is known (quranic:root_000224:B001/m01); unuttered inward speech (quranic:root_001272:B012/m01); deceptive redirection from a thing's face (quranic:root_000682:B002/m01); withholding from a right (quranic:root_000967:B008/m01); arrogant self-elevation (quranic:root_001042:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:13 `ب ص ر` (مُبْصِرَة), `ق و ل` (قَالُوا), and `س ح ر` (سِحْر); 27:14 `ي ق ن` (اسْتَيْقَنَتْهَا), `ن ف س` (أَنْفُسُهُمْ), `ج ح د` (جَحَدُوا), `ظ ل م` (ظُلْمًا), and `ع ل و` (عُلُوًّا).
- Synthesis: The decisive contrast is not ignorance versus information but an interrupted disclosure circuit. Sight and conscience have already received the sign; denial then holds back what the inward self has established and substitutes a deceptive public label.

### 2. P2 (27:15-44) - Nonhuman Intelligence Within Ordered Sovereignty
- Semantic invariant: A sovereign field is maintained by gathering, regulating, perceiving, and communicating across human and nonhuman collectives.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:17-22 presents the mustered host, the ant warning, and the bird's reconnaissance as linked operations of order and situational knowledge.
- Surprising reach: Tiny communal bodies and airborne scouts are not decorative fauna; their lexical actions supply restraint, shelter, fine perception, absence detection, and comprehensive reporting.

#### Subchannel A. A mixed host is gathered and held in ordered ranks
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Human, hidden, and avian contingents are driven toward one destination while a restraining authority keeps the front and rear coordinated.
- Active motifs: gathering and driving toward a destination (quranic:root_000324:B001/m01); mutually supporting host (quranic:root_000264:B001/m01); hidden jinn collective (quranic:root_000266:B005/m01); visible human collective (quranic:root_000059:B001/m01); airborne birds (quranic:root_000962:B001/m01); organized restraint of a host (quranic:root_001644:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:17 `ح ش ر` (حُشِرَ), `ج ن د` (جُنُودُهُ), `ج ن ن` (الْجِنّ), `ء ن س` (الْإِنْس), `ط ي ر` (الطَّيْر), and `و ز ع` (يُوزَعُون).
- Synthesis: Sovereignty appears as controlled plurality. Different orders of creature remain distinct, but gathering and restraint convert them into one directed formation rather than an undifferentiated crowd.

#### Subchannel B. A small colony warns, shelters, and avoids crushing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A minute communal speaker detects an approaching host, calls its group into dwellings, and names the mechanical danger of being broken underfoot.
- Active motifs: small gathered ants (quranic:root_001556:B001/m01); uttered warning (quranic:root_001272:B001/m01); entry into an interior (quranic:root_000464:B001/m01); inhabited dwelling (quranic:root_000726:B002/m01); dry matter broken into fragments (quranic:root_000337:B001/m01); fine awareness (quranic:root_000798:B005/m01); military host (quranic:root_000264:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:18 `ن م ل` (النَّمْل/نَمْلَة), `ق و ل` (قَالَت), `د خ ل` (ادْخُلُوا), `س ك ن` (مَسَاكِنَكُمْ), `ح ط م` (يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ), `ش ع ر` (يَشْعُرُون), and `ج ن د` (جُنُودُهُ).
- Synthesis: The scene scales imperial movement down to the vulnerability of brittle small bodies. Intelligence consists in sensing an unintentional threat early enough to convert exposed movement into protected dwelling.

#### Subchannel C. Absence is converted into a comprehensive, certain report
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Inspection detects a missing bird; after a measured delay, the absent scout returns with news that claims full informational enclosure and certainty.
- Active motifs: searching for what has gone missing (quranic:root_001168:B002/m01); flying scout (quranic:root_000962:B001/m01); hidden absence (quranic:root_001117:B001/m01); waiting in place (quranic:root_001437:B001/m01); consequential report (quranic:root_001464:B002/m01); certainty without doubt (quranic:root_001696:B001/m01); complete informational enclosure (quranic:root_000372:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:20 `ف ق د` (تَفَقَّد), `ط ي ر` (الطَّيْر), and `غ ي ب` (الْغَائِبِين); 27:22 `م ك ث` (مَكَث), `ن ب ء` (نَبَإ), `ي ق ن` (يَقِين), and `ح و ط` (أَحَطتُ/تُحِط).
- Synthesis: The missing member is not merely recovered. Delay becomes reconnaissance, and spatial absence returns as a bounded knowledge claim whose certainty can then be tested by sovereign inquiry.

### 3. P2 (27:15-44) - Authority Negotiated Through Council, Letter, and Gift
- Semantic invariant: Political authority tests proposals and objects by sending them through deliberation, delivery, reception, and return.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:28-37 stages a written summons, collective consultation, a diplomatic gift, and its rejected valuation.
- Surprising reach: Return is an epistemic operation: a reply, an envoy, or a gift comes back carrying a judgment about the sender's claim.

#### Subchannel A. Council speech is cut into a decision
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: An elite assembly gathers around a matter, requests judgment, weighs witnessed counsel and military capacity, and separates one actionable decision.
- Active motifs: council united around an opinion (quranic:root_001441:B002/m01); consultation and management of opinion (quranic:root_000051:B007/m01); requested judgment and answer (quranic:root_001130:B004/m01); decisive separation of a matter (quranic:root_001240:B010/m01); presence as witness (quranic:root_000822:B001/m01); mutual examination of a course (quranic:root_001520:B010/m01); negotiation (quranic:root_001272:B009/m01); gathered strength (quranic:root_001274:B001/m01); overpowering martial force (quranic:root_000079:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:32 `م ل ء` (الْمَلَأ), `ف ت ي` (أَفْتُونِي), `ء م ر` (أَمْرِي/أَمْرًا), `ق ط ع` (قَاطِعَة), and `ش ه د` (تَشْهَدُون); 27:33 `ق و ل` (قَالُوا), `ق و ي` (قُوَّة), `ب ء س` (بَأْس), `ن ظ ر` (فَانظُرِي), and `ء م ر` (تَأْمُرِين).
- Synthesis: Deliberation is neither passive talk nor immediate violence. The council supplies witnessed alternatives and force estimates; the ruler's task is the cutting operation that turns distributed opinion into a single course.

#### Subchannel B. A written summons travels and returns as diplomatic speech
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A written message is carried, cast before its recipients, read as honorable, and placed into a cycle of observation and reply.
- Active motifs: dispatch (quranic:root_000563:B001/m01); bearer and carried message (quranic:root_000563:B002/m01); written document (quranic:root_001283:B002/m01); casting an object to another (quranic:root_001372:B005/m01); waiting for an outcome (quranic:root_001520:B002/m01); returned speech (quranic:root_000544:B005/m01); honorable quality (quranic:root_001294:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:28-29 `ك ت ب` (كِتَابِي/كِتَاب), `ل ق ي` (أَلْقِه/أُلْقِي), and `ق و ل` (قَالَت); 27:29 `ك ر م` (كَرِيم); 27:35 `ر س ل` (مُرْسِلَة/الْمُرْسَلُون), `ن ظ ر` (فَنَاظِرَة), and `ر ج ع` (يَرْجِع).
- Synthesis: Writing gives the command a portable body, while casting and waiting separate issuance from reception. The message's force is disclosed only after another court reads, deliberates, and returns a response.

#### Subchannel C. A gift attempts to convert conflict into exchange
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A diplomatic gift carries wealth and hoped-for attachment, but refusal returns it and replaces monetary valuation with a claim of superior divine good.
- Active motifs: relational gift (quranic:root_001583:B004/m01); accumulated wealth (quranic:root_001457:B001/m01); material support added to another (quranic:root_001407:B002/m01); beneficial good (quranic:root_000452:B001/m01); generosity and gift (quranic:root_000452:B005/m01); exultant, misplaced joy (quranic:root_001140:B002/m01); return to the sender (quranic:root_000544:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:35-36 `ه د ي` (هَدِيَّة/هَدِيَّتِكُمْ); 27:36 `م و ل` (مَال), `م د د` (أَتُمِدُّونَنِ), `خ ي ر` (خَيْر), and `ف ر ح` (تَفْرَحُون); 27:37 `ر ج ع` (ارْجِع).
- Synthesis: The object is an attempted medium of allegiance, not a neutral present. Its return breaks the proposed exchange rate: wealth cannot purchase the receiving sovereign, and the failed gift comes back as evidence about both courts.

### 4. P2 (27:15-44) - The Throne as a Measure of Power, Recognition, and Gratitude
- Semantic invariant: The throne is repeatedly moved, re-presented, and interpreted so that authority becomes measurable through timing, transport, recognition, and response.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:38-42 compares transport capacities, settles the throne before the eye returns, alters its appearance, and tests recognition.
- Surprising reach: Throne vocabulary also forms a mounted conveyance scene, recasting the elevated seat as a woman's canopy or howdah in motion.

#### Subchannel A. Competing transport claims are measured by bodily intervals
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Two claimants promise to bring the royal seat before bodily thresholds, standing from a place and the return of an eye-blink, after which the object is seen stably present.
- Active motifs: elevated royal seat (quranic:root_001000:B001/m01); coming or bringing into presence (quranic:root_000009:B001/m01); temporal precedence (quranic:root_001198:B002/m01); bodily rising (quranic:root_001273:B002/m01); gathered capacity (quranic:root_001274:B001/m01); trusted security (quranic:root_000054:B001/m01); return to position (quranic:root_000555:B001/m01); blink of the eye (quranic:root_000931:B002/m01); stable placement (quranic:root_001215:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:38-40 `ع ر ش` (عَرْشَهَا), `ء ت ي` (يَأْتِينِي/ءَاتِيكَ), and `ق ب ل` (قَبْل); 27:39 `ق و م` (تَقُوم/مَقَامِكَ), `ق و ي` (قَوِيّ), and `ء م ن` (أَمِين); 27:40 `ر د د` (يَرْتَدَّ), `ط ر ف` (طَرْفُكَ), and `ق ر ر` (مُسْتَقِرًّا).
- Synthesis: Power is expressed through elapsed bodily action rather than an abstract boast. One claim uses the duration of standing; the stronger event fits inside a blink and is verified by the throne's settled presence.

#### Subchannel B. The royal seat becomes a mounted canopy
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: The throne image shifts into a woman's canopy or howdah carried by a mount, giving transport a concrete vehicle-frame.
- Active motifs: woman's canopy on a camel (quranic:root_001000:B005/m01); mounted howdah (quranic:root_001215:B004/m01); movement of mounts toward saddles (quranic:root_000762:B009/m01); brought arrival (quranic:root_000009:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:38-42 `ع ر ش` (عَرْشَهَا/عَرْشُكِ); 27:40,44 `ق ر ر` (مُسْتَقِرًّا/قَوَارِير); 27:44 `س و ق` (سَاقَيْهَا); 27:38-40 `ء ت ي` (يَأْتِينِي/ءَاتِيكَ).
- Synthesis: The canopy and howdah senses produce a complete transport scene: an elevated female-associated seat is borne on a conveyance. This does not reduce the extraordinary arrival to ordinary travel, but it gives the otherwise instantaneous transfer a latent material chassis.

#### Subchannel C. Alteration tests recognition rather than mere eyesight
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A familiar throne is changed toward unfamiliarity, presented for inspection, and used to distinguish visual resemblance from guided recognition.
- Active motifs: alteration into the unknown (quranic:root_001550:B004/m01); royal throne (quranic:root_001000:B001/m01); directed visual examination (quranic:root_001520:B001/m01); gentle guidance to truth (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01); knowledge becoming disclosed (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01); prior state (quranic:root_001198:B002/m01); occurring state (quranic:root_001332:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:41 `ن ك ر` (نَكِّرُوا), `ع ر ش` (عَرْشَهَا), `ن ظ ر` (نَنظُر), and `ه د ي` (أَتَهْتَدِي); 27:42 `ع ر ش` (عَرْشُكِ), `ع ل م` (الْعِلْم), `ق ب ل` (قَبْلِهَا), and `ك و ن` (كُنَّا).
- Synthesis: The test operates between sameness and difference. Alteration prevents automatic naming, so the response must negotiate memory, resemblance, prior knowledge, and willingness to be guided.

#### Subchannel D. Settled possession becomes a trial of gratitude
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Once the throne is settled, possession is reclassified as unowed favor whose proper outcome is gratitude rather than self-sufficient ownership.
- Active motifs: settled presence (quranic:root_001215:B003/m01); unowed favor (quranic:root_001163:B003/m01); trial that reveals quality (quranic:root_000153:B002/m01); grateful recognition (quranic:root_000810:B001/m01); covering a benefit (quranic:root_001307:B004/m01); the self as the acting beneficiary (quranic:root_001533:B012/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:40 `ق ر ر` (مُسْتَقِرًّا), `ف ض ل` (فَضْل), `ب ل و` (لِيَبْلُوَنِي), `ش ك ر` (أَشْكُر/شَكَر), `ك ف ر` (أَكْفُر/كَفَر), and `ن ف س` (نَفْسِهِ).
- Synthesis: Arrival does not terminate the scene. The stable object initiates a moral assay: gratitude discloses the gift as gift, while ingratitude covers that relation and harms only the ungrateful self.

### 5. P2 (27:15-44) - Perception Redirected by Concealment, Ornament, and Surface
- Semantic invariant: What is hidden or cosmetically presented governs orientation until an extraction, disclosure, or corrected look restores the underlying relation.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:24-25 contrasts ornamented misdirection with hidden things brought forth, while 27:44 resolves a transparent surface mistaken for deep water.
- Surprising reach: Concealment ranges from buried stores and inward intention to political-religious ornament and optically deceptive architecture.

#### Subchannel A. Hidden deposits are brought from storage into declared knowledge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A stored or buried thing moves from concealment in fertile earth into extraction, visibility, and a field where hidden and public states are equally known.
- Active motifs: hidden storage (quranic:root_000384:B001/m01); buried cultivation deposits (quranic:root_000384:B007/m01); extraction from concealment (quranic:root_000400:B002/m01); hidden state (quranic:root_000428:B001/m01); public manifestation (quranic:root_001041:B001/m01); knowledge disclosed to the knower (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01); fertile ground (quranic:root_000025:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:25 `خ ب ء` (الْخَبْءَ), `خ ر ج` (يُخْرِج), `خ ف ي` (تُخْفُون), `ع ل ن` (تُعْلِنُون), `ع ل م` (يَعْلَم), and `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض).
- Synthesis: The hidden thing is not an empty abstraction. Storage and cultivation senses make it a retained deposit with a location, while extraction and declaration move it into a knowledge relation.

#### Subchannel B. Ornament redirects prostration away from its path
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Displayed beauty makes a misoriented practice appear fitting, blocks a traversable route, and transfers bodily submission to a luminous but subordinate object.
- Active motifs: cosmetic enhancement (quranic:root_000660:B002/m01); turning and blocking (quranic:root_000848:B001/m01); traversable path (quranic:root_000672:B001/m01); guidance toward truth (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01); bodily abasement (quranic:root_000675:B001/m01); solar disk and light (quranic:root_000818:B001/m01); a subordinate other (quranic:root_000502:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:24 `ز ي ن` (زَيَّن), `ص د د` (فَصَدَّهُمْ), `س ب ل` (السَّبِيل), `ه د ي` (يَهْتَدُون), `س ج د` (يَسْجُدُون), `ش م س` (الشَّمْس), and `د و ن` (مِن دُونِ); 27:25 `س ج د` (يَسْجُدُوا).
- Synthesis: The failure is directional. Ornament modifies appearance, appearance redirects prostration, and the blocked path prevents the body from reaching the relation that its act of submission should express.

#### Subchannel C. A polished glass floor is mistaken for deep water, then exposed
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A high polished structure presents an optically open surface; the viewer estimates it as a sea-depth, uncovers her legs, and then receives an explicit architectural correction.
- Active motifs: high palace structure (quranic:root_000854:B004/m01); truth brought into the open (quranic:root_000854:B001/m01); visual perception (quranic:root_000531:B001/m01); non-certain estimation (quranic:root_000318:B002/m01); deep sea-water (quranic:root_001344:B002/m01); polished smooth surface (quranic:root_001413:B002/m01); fragile transparent glass (quranic:root_001215:B012/m01); removal of a covering (quranic:root_001302:B001/m01); bodily leg (quranic:root_000762:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:44 `ص ر ح` (الصَّرْح/صَرْح), `ر ء ي` (رَأَتْه), `ح س ب` (حَسِبَتْه), `ل ج ج` (لُجَّة), `م ر د` (مُمَرَّد), `ق ر ر` (قَوَارِير), `ك ش ف` (كَشَفَت), and `س و ق` (سَاقَيْهَا).
- Synthesis: The surface does not hide by opacity but by excessive optical openness. The body's defensive response exposes the mistaken estimate, and verbal clarification finally aligns visible surface, material construction, and meaning.

### 6. P3 (27:45-58) - Collective Speech Hardening Into Conspiracy
- Semantic invariant: Speech progressively binds separated people into an antagonistic collective, then supplies the oath and counterfeit account by which that collective tries to control action and memory.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:45 opens with two disputing factions, and 27:48-49 condenses nine close men into a sworn night plan and a prepared denial.
- Surprising reach: The same language that can negotiate or reconcile becomes an instrument for consolidating violence and manufacturing an account after the event.

#### Subchannel A. A community separates into disputing parties
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A people divides into distinct groups whose speech takes the form of adversarial negotiation rather than reconciliation.
- Active motifs: separated faction (quranic:root_001148:B005/m01); dispute between opponents (quranic:root_000416:B001/m01); negotiation over a matter (quranic:root_001272:B009/m01); social group (quranic:root_001273:B001/m01); reconciliation that removes estrangement (quranic:root_000876:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:45 `ف ر ق` (فَرِيقَان), `خ ص م` (يَخْتَصِمُون), and `ص ل ح` (صَالِحًا); 27:46 `ق و ل` (قَال) and `ق و م` (يَا قَوْم).
- Synthesis: Division is enacted through speech. The latent reconciliation sense establishes the unrealized alternative, while faction and dispute show a community whose communicative relation has hardened into opposed camps.

#### Subchannel B. Nine close men consolidate resolve through oath and night planning
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A small male kin-group gathers scattered intentions into one resolve, divides an oath among itself, and schedules the attack under cover of night.
- Active motifs: number nine (quranic:root_000181:B001/m01); close male band (quranic:root_000605:B001/m01); collective resolve after divided opinions (quranic:root_000259:B003/m01); distributed oath (quranic:root_001226:B004/m01); nocturnal action and planning (quranic:root_000166:B004/m01); household affiliation (quranic:root_000064:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:48 `ت س ع` (تِسْعَة), `ر ه ط` (رَهْط), and the city setting; 27:49 `ق س م` (تَقَاسَمُوا), `ب ي ت` (لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ), and `ء ه ل` (أَهْلَهُ); 27:51 `ج م ع` (أَجْمَعِين).
- Synthesis: The conspiracy is a social assembly mechanism. Number and kinship delimit the actors, collective resolve closes deliberation, the oath distributes liability, and night planning converts solidarity into coordinated violence.

#### Subchannel C. A fabricated witness statement is prepared before the killing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The conspirators precompose a denial for the victim's guardian, presenting absence from the event as witnessed fact and naming the false account truthful.
- Active motifs: witnessed presence (quranic:root_000822:B001/m01); testimony that claims decisive knowledge (quranic:root_000822:B002/m01); attribution of words or events that did not occur (quranic:root_001272:B005/m01); truthful correspondence between claim and event (quranic:root_000852:B001/m01); guardian responsible for an affair (quranic:root_001684:B003/m01); death and disappearance (quranic:root_001596:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:49 `ق و ل` (لَنَقُولَنَّ), `و ل ي` (لِوَلِيِّهِ), `ش ه د` (مَا شَهِدْنَا), `ه ل ك` (مَهْلِكَ), and `ص د ق` (لَصَادِقُون).
- Synthesis: Testimony is inverted before the crime occurs. The group plans not merely an attack but the evidentiary frame that will follow it, using the vocabulary of witness and truth to erase its own presence.

### 7. P3 (27:45-58) - Selective Removal Reordering Houses and Households
- Semantic invariant: Judgment separates a population by extracting some, leaving residue, and emptying or destroying the structures that held the condemned.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:51-58 moves from collective destruction and vacant houses to two rescues, one remaining wife, and a punitive rain.
- Surprising reach: Rescue is materialized as separation, scraping, and removal, while destruction is measured by what remains: empty dwellings, a residual person, or exposed ground under falling water.

#### Subchannel A. Destruction leaves houses empty and collapsed
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A planned killing reverses into comprehensive destruction whose visible outcome is dwellings emptied of their people and fallen from their support.
- Active motifs: exterminating destruction (quranic:root_000487:B002/m01); death and disappearance (quranic:root_001596:B001/m01); vacancy (quranic:root_000450:B001/m01); collapse (quranic:root_000450:B002/m01); dwelling (quranic:root_000166:B001/m01); household (quranic:root_000166:B002/m01); consequential outcome (quranic:root_001033:B006/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:49 `ه ل ك` (مَهْلِكَ); 27:51 `د م ر` (دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ) and `ع ق ب` (عَاقِبَة); 27:52 `ب ي ت` (بُيُوتُهُمْ) and `خ و ي` (خَاوِيَة).
- Synthesis: The outcome is architectural as well as mortal. Erasure of the group becomes legible in structures that persist only as vacant or collapsed containers of a former household.

#### Subchannel B. Believers are extracted behind a protective boundary
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A believing group is separated out of danger, brought beyond the threatened social enclosure, and held behind a protective relation.
- Active motifs: escape by separation (quranic:root_001476:B001/m01); scraping or extracting a thing free (quranic:root_001476:B003/m01); emergence from an enclosing state (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01); protective barrier against harm (quranic:root_001677:B001/m01); inward assent to truth (quranic:root_000054:B002/m01); household bond (quranic:root_000064:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:53 `ن ج و` (أَنجَيْنَا), `ء م ن` (ءَامَنُوا), and `و ق ي` (يَتَّقُون); 27:56 `خ ر ج` (أَخْرِجُوا); 27:57 `ن ج و` (أَنجَيْنَاهُ) and `ء ه ل` (أَهْلَهُ).
- Synthesis: Salvation is not a vague favorable result. The lexical assembly gives it the mechanics of extraction: a bounded group is pulled free from the condemned field and placed behind protection.

#### Subchannel C. One wife remains as the designated residue
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A household is removed, but one woman is measured into the remainder and stays after the others have gone.
- Active motifs: residue left after departure (quranic:root_001071:B001/m01); woman (quranic:root_001410:B001/m01); deliberate measured arrangement (quranic:root_001205:B005/m01); household bond (quranic:root_000064:B001/m01); escape by separation (quranic:root_001476:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:57 `ن ج و` (أَنجَيْنَاهُ), `ء ه ل` (أَهْلَهُ), `م ر ء` (امْرَأَتَهُ), `ق د ر` (قَدَّرْنَاهَا), and `غ ب ر` (الْغَابِرِين).
- Synthesis: The exception is expressed as a residue operation. Household membership alone does not determine removal; measured assignment distinguishes the person who remains from the household that escapes.

#### Subchannel D. Punitive rain exposes and overwhelms the warned
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Water descends from above not as provision but as an assault upon an exposed population already placed under warning.
- Active motifs: falling rainwater (quranic:root_001431:B001/m01); rain specified as punishment (quranic:root_001431:B002/m01); exposure to what descends (quranic:root_001431:B003/m01); distressing evil (quranic:root_000755:B002/m01); warning that awakens caution (quranic:root_001488:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:58 `م ط ر` (أَمْطَرْنَا/مَطَرًا/مَطَر), `س و ء` (فَسَاء), and `ن ذ ر` (الْمُنذَرِين).
- Synthesis: Rain's ordinary beneficent operation is reversed. Descent, exposure, and warning remain intact, but the water now executes removal rather than growth.

### 8. P3 (27:45-58) - Transgressed Relation and Contested Cleansing
- Semantic invariant: Bodies and communities are judged by how desire crosses a relational limit and by whether cleansing is treated as restoration or grounds for expulsion.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:54-57 names visible transgression, displaced desire, the community's hostility to purification, expulsion, and rescue.
- Surprising reach: Cleansing is made bodily concrete through washing, waste removal, and scraping, linking moral purification to the same extraction mechanics used by rescue.

#### Subchannel A. Appetite bypasses its counterpart and exceeds a limit
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Desire moves toward men while passing women by, converting appetite into a relational act that exceeds its assigned measure.
- Active motifs: appetite directed toward an object (quranic:root_000825:B001/m01); adult male (quranic:root_000546:B002/m01); collective of women (quranic:root_001500:B001/m01); substitution by an other (quranic:root_000502:B003/m01); exceeding a limit (quranic:root_001134:B002/m01); impulsive action against what is right (quranic:root_000271:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:54 `ف ح ش` (الْفَاحِشَة) and perception of the act; 27:55 `ش ه و` (شَهْوَة), `ر ج ل` (الرِّجَال), `د و ن` (مِن دُون), `ن س و` (النِّسَاء), and `ج ه ل` (تَجْهَلُون).
- Synthesis: The scene's structure is not appetite alone but redirected relation. The “other/besides” motif marks the bypass, while excess and impulsive disorder characterize the resulting act.

#### Subchannel B. Purification is recoded as a reason for civic expulsion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: People characterized by removing moral stain are rhetorically marked as outsiders and driven from the inhabited community.
- Active motifs: purification of self and conduct (quranic:root_000953:B005/m01); forced emergence from a place (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01); gathered settlement (quranic:root_001222:B001/m01); human persons (quranic:root_000059:B001/m01); public utterance (quranic:root_001272:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:56 `ق و ل` (قَالُوا), `خ ر ج` (أَخْرِجُوا), `ق ر ي` (قَرْيَتِكُمْ), `ء ن س` (أُنَاس), and `ط ه ر` (يَتَطَهَّرُون).
- Synthesis: The community reverses moral polarity through speech. Cleansing becomes deviance, and the city tries to preserve itself by expelling the very people whose defining action is removal of corruption.

#### Subchannel C. Cleansing operates as washing, waste removal, and extraction
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Impurity is washed away, bodily waste is removed, and adhered material is scraped free, forming a concrete extraction model for purification and rescue.
- Active motifs: washing purification (quranic:root_000953:B003/m01); removal of bodily waste (quranic:root_001476:B006/m01); scraping and extraction (quranic:root_001476:B003/m01); emergence from confinement (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:53,57 `ن ج و` (أَنجَيْنَا/أَنجَيْنَاهُ); 27:56 `ط ه ر` (يَتَطَهَّرُون) and `خ ر ج` (أَخْرِجُوا).
- Synthesis: The shared removal mechanics make cleansing tangible: wash, evacuate, scrape, and bring outside. This bodily channel sharpens the contrast between a community that expels purifiers and a judgment that extracts them from danger.

### 9. P4 (27:59-75) - Water Ordered Through Descent, Enclosure, Channel, and Barrier
- Semantic invariant: Water becomes life-bearing and habitable when its movement is directed through distinct vertical, generative, lateral, and separating operations.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:60-61 moves from rain to gardens, then to settled earth, internal rivers, fixed mountains, and a barrier between seas.
- Surprising reach: The cosmic hydrology can be miniaturized into a vessel scene in which water is poured, received, and held.

#### Subchannel A. Water descends from the upper cover into fertile ground
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Water is sent downward from the overhanging sky, arrives in the lower fertile ground, and functions as apportioned life-giving provision.
- Active motifs: downward descent (quranic:root_001492:B001/m01); caused delivery from above (quranic:root_001492:B002/m01); water substance (quranic:root_001458:B001/m01); abundant visible water (quranic:root_001458:B002/m01); upper covering sky (quranic:root_000745:B004/m01); fertile earth (quranic:root_000025:B002/m01); rain as provision (quranic:root_000560:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:60 `ن ز ل` (أَنزَل), `س م و` (السَّمَاء), `م و ه` (مَاء), and `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض); 27:64 `ر ز ق` (يَرْزُقُكُم) and sky/earth provision.
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes source, direction, material, receiver, and function. Rain is not merely “water”; it is an apportioned transfer from an upper cover into ground capable of receiving life.

#### Subchannel B. Germination fills an enclosed garden with visible delight
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Water activates planted matter, which emerges as stalked trees inside an encircling garden and culminates in freshness and delight.
- Active motifs: plant emerging from earth (quranic:root_001465:B001/m01); deliberate planting (quranic:root_001465:B002/m01); enclosure around a plot (quranic:root_000300:B001/m01); walled garden (quranic:root_000300:B003/m01); stalked tree (quranic:root_000777:B001/m01); freshness and beauty (quranic:root_000158:B001/m01); delight (quranic:root_000158:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:60 `ن ب ت` (فَأَنبَتْنَا/تُنبِتُوا), `ح د ق` (حَدَائِق), `ش ج ر` (شَجَرَهَا), and `ب ه ج` (بَهْجَة).
- Synthesis: Growth is a staged construction: planted material exits the earth, develops a supporting stalk, fills a bounded plot, and presents a perceptible outcome of freshness and joy.

#### Subchannel C. Rivers open paths through a settled, anchored earth
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Stable ground receives internal openings through which water cuts and widens channels, while anchored masses preserve the larger terrain.
- Active motifs: lower ground (quranic:root_000025:B001/m01); stable placement (quranic:root_001215:B003/m01); smooth settled basin (quranic:root_001215:B006/m01); gap between things (quranic:root_000435:B001/m01); river cutting through earth (quranic:root_001559:B001/m01); widening until flow is possible (quranic:root_001559:B003/m01); fixed anchorage (quranic:root_000564:B001/m01); making a thing present (quranic:root_000248:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:61 `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض), `ق ر ر` (قَرَارًا), `خ ل ل` (خِلَالَهَا), `ن ه ر` (أَنْهَارًا), `ر س و` (رَوَاسِي), and repeated `ج ع ل` (جَعَل).
- Synthesis: Habitability depends on paired operations rather than uniform solidity. Some structures hold fast; others open, cut, and widen so that flow can pass through the fixed field without dissolving it.

#### Subchannel D. A separator prevents two broad waters from merging
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Two expansive bodies of water face one another across a middle interval held by an effective dividing structure.
- Active motifs: broad abundant water (quranic:root_000086:B001/m01); middle interval (quranic:root_000170:B002/m01); relational connection between sides (quranic:root_000170:B003/m01); preventing separator (quranic:root_000297:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:61 `ب ح ر` (الْبَحْرَيْن), `ب ي ن` (بَيْن), and `ح ج ز` (حَاجِزًا).
- Synthesis: The barrier does not erase relation; it regulates it. “Between” holds both separation and connection, while the separator gives that middle an active capacity to prevent indiscriminate mixing.

#### Subchannel E. Cosmic water movement contracts into pouring and receiving
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Water is conveyed by pouring into a large receiving vessel and held there as a bounded quantity.
- Active motifs: water delivered by pouring (quranic:root_001458:B003/m01); a single pour into a vessel (quranic:root_001215:B005/m01); large jar (quranic:root_001251:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:60 `م و ه` (مَاء); 27:61 `ق ر ر` (قَرَارًا); 27:62 `ق ل ل` (قَلِيلًا).
- Synthesis: The vessel scene preserves the same roles as the larger landscape: directed transfer, receiving cavity, retained contents, and measured amount. It materializes cosmic provision as a controlled act of filling.

### 10. P4 (27:59-75) - Navigation by Terrain, Advance Signs, and Historical Trace
- Semantic invariant: Guidance proceeds by reading directional media before, within, and after movement: terrain, weather signs, and the visible outcomes left by prior travelers.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:63 names guidance in land and sea and winds sent before mercy, while 27:69 commands travel and inspection of outcomes.
- Surprising reach: An unknown trackless land is the negative image of guidance, and historical consequence becomes a navigational trace rather than only a moral abstraction.

#### Subchannel A. Guidance makes land and sea traversable
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Direction is supplied across dry land and ridden water, opposed by an unmarked terrain in which no route can be found.
- Active motifs: gentle direction toward a route (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01); course and bearing (quranic:root_001583:B002/m01); dry land (quranic:root_000104:B005/m01); sea travel (quranic:root_000086:B009/m01); trackless unknown ground (quranic:root_001049:B006/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:63 `ه د ي` (يَهْدِيكُمْ), `ب ر ر` (الْبَرّ), and `ب ح ر` (الْبَحْر); 27:66 `ع م ي` (عَمُون) supplies the local blindness/tracklessness pressure.
- Synthesis: Guidance is a practical relation among traveler, bearing, and traversable medium. The trackless-land sense gives non-guidance a spatial form: not simply error, but a place without usable marks.

#### Subchannel B. Sent winds announce mercy before its arrival
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Moving air is dispatched as an advance signal whose perceptible onset precedes and announces a merciful event.
- Active motifs: dispatch and release (quranic:root_000563:B001/m01); moving wind (quranic:root_000609:B003/m01); first signs and heralds (quranic:root_000120:B007/m01); what stands immediately before an event (quranic:root_001693:B008/m01); mercy and beneficence (quranic:root_000552:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:63 `ر س ل` (يُرْسِل), `ر و ح` (الرِّيَاح), `ب ش ر` (بُشْرًا), `ي د ي` (بَيْنَ يَدَيْ), and `ر ح م` (رَحْمَتِهِ).
- Synthesis: The wind is both moving material and readable message. Its arrival before rain converts atmospheric motion into temporal orientation toward mercy.

#### Subchannel C. Travel reads the surviving trace of prior action
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A traveler crosses the land, directs sight toward material remains, and infers the consequential endpoint of criminal action.
- Active motifs: forward travel (quranic:root_000769:B001/m01); traveled way or conduct (quranic:root_000769:B002/m01); ground traversed (quranic:root_000025:B001/m01); directed inspection (quranic:root_001520:B001/m01); consequential endpoint (quranic:root_001033:B006/m01); crime and culpability (quranic:root_000239:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:69 `س ي ر` (سِيرُوا), `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض), `ن ظ ر` (فَانظُرُوا), `ع ق ب` (عَاقِبَة), and `ج ر م` (الْمُجْرِمِين).
- Synthesis: History becomes navigable evidence. Movement supplies access, sight reads the trace, and “outcome” identifies the terminus toward which a prior mode of conduct traveled.

### 11. P4 (27:59-75) - Constraint Opened Into Relief and Succession
- Semantic invariant: A constrained person is moved from compulsion through response and release into renewed capacity or placement.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:62 joins the compelled caller, answered appeal, removal of harm, and installation of successors in the earth.
- Surprising reach: Relief and political succession share an opening mechanism: what was trapped is released, and a newly capable occupant takes a place.

#### Subchannel A. The compelled caller receives an answer and an uncovering
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Necessity drives a person to call; a reply reaches the caller and lifts the covering condition of harm.
- Active motifs: coercive necessity (quranic:root_000907:B003/m01); vocal appeal (quranic:root_000478:B001/m01); responsive answer (quranic:root_000273:B003/m01); lifting a cover or distress (quranic:root_001302:B001/m01); experienced harm (quranic:root_000755:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:62 `ض ر ر` (الْمُضْطَر), `د ع و` (دَعَاه), `ج و ب` (يُجِيب), `ك ش ف` (يَكْشِف), and `س و ء` (السُّوء).
- Synthesis: The sequence is operationally exact: compulsion narrows agency, the call opens a communicative line, response crosses it, and uncovering removes the condition that had enclosed the caller.

#### Subchannel B. Successors are installed into an available earthly place
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A later occupant is made to take the place of a prior one and is established within the earthly field.
- Active motifs: transformation into a new status (quranic:root_000248:B002/m01); successor replacing what has gone (quranic:root_000433:B001/m01); standing in another's place (quranic:root_001273:B007/m01); earthly ground (quranic:root_000025:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:62 `ج ع ل` (يَجْعَلُكُمْ), `خ ل ف` (خُلَفَاء), and `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض); 27:60 `ق و م` (قَوْم) supplies the local standing-community anchor for the latent replacement sense.
- Synthesis: Succession is a placement operation, not only chronology. The new group receives a vacated position and the capacity to stand where another had stood.

### 12. P4 (27:59-75) - Hidden Interior Made Legible
- Semantic invariant: Concealed matter becomes accountable when it is declared, written, excavated, or tested against a distinguishing sign.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:64-66 and 27:74-75 contrast proof and doubt, hidden interiors and public declaration, and absent things with a clear written record.
- Surprising reach: The unseen is also botanical: seed is covered, roots disappear below ground, and growth later makes the hidden deposit visible.

#### Subchannel A. What the chest protects is opposed to public declaration
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An interior container preserves unspoken content, while declaration moves that content into public visibility and knowledge.
- Active motifs: protective concealment (quranic:root_001324:B001/m01); content hidden in the self (quranic:root_001324:B002/m01); bodily chest (quranic:root_000849:B001/m01); source from which action issues (quranic:root_000849:B004/m01); public manifestation (quranic:root_001041:B001/m01); disclosed knowledge (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:74 `ك ن ن` (تُكِنُّ), `ص د ر` (صُدُورُهُمْ), `ع ل ن` (يُعْلِنُون), and `ع ل م` (يَعْلَم).
- Synthesis: The chest is both body cavity and action-source. Concealment protects an inward intention before it issues outward; declaration reverses that direction and makes the content publicly knowable.

#### Subchannel B. Every absent item is fixed in a clarifying record
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Whatever is hidden from sight in the upper and lower realms is entered into a written determination that renders it locatable and explicit.
- Active motifs: absence from sight and knowledge (quranic:root_001117:B001/m01); written document (quranic:root_001283:B002/m01); binding written determination (quranic:root_001283:B003/m01); emergence into clarity (quranic:root_000170:B004/m01); meaning disclosed in writing (quranic:root_000170:B005/m01); upper covering realm (quranic:root_000745:B004/m01); lower earthly realm (quranic:root_000025:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:65 `غ ي ب` (الْغَيْب), `س م و` (السَّمَاوَات), and `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض); 27:75 `غ ي ب` (غَائِبَة), `س م و` (السَّمَاء), `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض), `ك ت ب` (كِتَاب), and `ب ي ن` (مُبِين).
- Synthesis: The record does more than store information. Writing fixes a determination, and clarification turns “absent” from an epistemic void into an item with an ordered place in a complete account.

#### Subchannel C. Covered seed and hidden roots return as visible growth
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A cultivator covers seed with soil; roots remain hidden below, then plant matter exits the earth and presents fresh shoots.
- Active motifs: covering seed with earth (quranic:root_001307:B008/m01); buried roots (quranic:root_001117:B008/m01); extraction from concealment (quranic:root_000400:B002/m01); plant emerging from earth (quranic:root_001465:B001/m01); soil and dust (quranic:root_000178:B001/m01); fresh shoot (quranic:root_000810:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:60 `ن ب ت` (أَنبَتْنَا); 27:65,75 `غ ي ب` (الْغَيْب/غَائِبَة); 27:67 `ك ف ر` (كَفَرُوا), `ت ر ب` (تُرَابًا), and `خ ر ج` (مُخْرَجُون); 27:73 `ش ك ر` (يَشْكُرُون).
- Synthesis: The botanical cycle supplies a material analogue for hidden knowledge and resurrection: concealment is an active sowing stage, not final absence, and emergence reveals what persisted below the visible surface.

#### Subchannel D. Doubt and tracklessness yield to knowledge and proof
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Confused alternatives and an unmarked route obstruct arrival at certainty until knowledge catches up and a distinguishing proof is produced.
- Active motifs: interpenetrating alternatives without certainty (quranic:root_000812:B001/m01); blindness of insight (quranic:root_001049:B002/m01); trackless terrain (quranic:root_001049:B006/m01); catching and reaching (quranic:root_000471:B001/m01); disclosed knowledge (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01); demonstrative proof (quranic:root_000112:B001/m01); truthful claim (quranic:root_000852:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:64 `ب ر ه ن` (بُرْهَانَكُمْ) and `ص د ق` (صَادِقِين); 27:65-66 `ع ل م` (يَعْلَم/عِلْمُهُمْ), `د ر ك` (ادَّارَكَ), `ش ك ك` (شَك), and `ع م ي` (عَمُون).
- Synthesis: Epistemic failure is figured as both entanglement and failed navigation. Proof supplies a differentiating mark; knowledge “catches up” to what doubt and blindness could not traverse.

### 13. P4 (27:59-75) - Beginning, Return, and the Event Following Close Behind
- Semantic invariant: Origins are intelligible only with their continuations: created things return, prior generations become present evidence, and a promised event advances behind the hearer.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:64 and 27:67-72 join beginning and re-creation, ancestral dust, prior promises, and an approaching event.
- Surprising reach: Temporal distance is repeatedly spatialized as advance, return to a place, emergence from soil, and a follower riding close behind.

#### Subchannel A. Measured creation begins, returns, and is provisioned
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A maker measures and originates created things, brings them back after departure, and apportions the sustenance by which they continue.
- Active motifs: prior measuring (quranic:root_000434:B001/m01); originating creation (quranic:root_000434:B002/m01); beginning followed by return (quranic:root_000090:B002/m01); return after departure (quranic:root_001058:B001/m01); destination of return (quranic:root_001058:B002/m01); apportioned provision (quranic:root_000560:B001/m01); consumed sustenance (quranic:root_000560:B002/m01); rain provision (quranic:root_000560:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:60,64 `خ ل ق` (خَلَق/الْخَلْق); 27:64 `ب د ء` (يَبْدَأ), `ع و د` (يُعِيدُ), and `ر ز ق` (يَرْزُقُكُمْ).
- Synthesis: Origination is not isolated manufacture. Measuring precedes making, return doubles the beginning, and provision sustains the created field between those two acts.

#### Subchannel B. Dust and ancestors become the material of denied emergence
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A present generation projects backward to its fathers and downward to dust, then rejects the prospect that those buried beginnings can come outside again.
- Active motifs: soil and mortal dust (quranic:root_000178:B001/m01); fatherhood and generation (quranic:root_000007:B001/m01); temporal precedence (quranic:root_001198:B002/m01); firstness (quranic:root_000067:B001/m01); emergence from confinement (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:67 `ت ر ب` (تُرَابًا), `ء ب و` (ءَابَاؤُنَا), and `خ ر ج` (مُخْرَجُون); 27:68 `ء ب و` (ءَابَاؤُنَا), `ق ب ل` (مِن قَبْل), and `ء و ل` (الْأَوَّلِين).
- Synthesis: The objection depends on treating dust as terminal and ancestry as remote. Emergence reverses both assumptions: what went below can come out, and what belongs to “the first” can bear upon the present.

#### Subchannel C. The promised event rides immediately behind the impatient
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A temporally fixed promise approaches as a follower from behind, while impatient demand tries to pull part of it forward before its time.
- Active motifs: promise opening expectation (quranic:root_001662:B001/m01); appointed time or place (quranic:root_001662:B003/m01); following closely after (quranic:root_000556:B001/m01); hasty advancement (quranic:root_000987:B001/m01); a part taken from a whole (quranic:root_000133:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:68,71 `و ع د` (وُعِدْنَا/الْوَعْد); 27:72 `ر د ف` (رَدِفَ), `ع ج ل` (تَسْتَعْجِلُون), and `ب ع ض` (بَعْض).
- Synthesis: The promise is neither absent nor stationary. It is spatially close and following, whereas impatience attempts to reverse the proper sequence by demanding an early fragment of what is already advancing.

### 14. P5 (27:76-93) - Speech Testing the Capacity to Receive
- Semantic invariant: A communicative act reveals or changes its receiver's capacity: recitation can guide, closed hearing can refuse, a creature can speak, and a trumpet can compel universal response.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:76-87 moves through Qur'anic narration, failed and successful hearing, the speaking earth-creature, and the trumpet blast.
- Surprising reach: Communication is repeatedly embodied as following sound, sealed openings, hidden crawling motion, breath filling an instrument, and involuntary arrival.

#### Subchannel A. Recitation follows the trace of disputed history
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Recited text tracks an inherited dispute step by step, orders its reports, and converts the traced account into clarification, guidance, and mercy.
- Active motifs: recitation and instruction (quranic:root_001210:B002/m01); following in sequence (quranic:root_000186:B001/m01); one sound following another (quranic:root_000186:B007/m01); tracking an imprint (quranic:root_001232:B001/m01); ordered narration (quranic:root_001232:B002/m01); disclosure through language (quranic:root_000170:B005/m01); guidance toward truth (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01); merciful beneficence (quranic:root_000552:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:76 `ق ر ء` (الْقُرْءَان), `ق ص ص` (يَقُصُّ), and the disputed matter; 27:77 `ه د ي` (هُدًى) and `ر ح م` (رَحْمَة); 27:79 `ب ي ن` (الْمُبِين); 27:92 `ت ل و` (أَتْلُو) and `ق ر ء` (الْقُرْءَان).
- Synthesis: Narration is a disciplined following operation. The recitation retraces a contested sequence and makes its relations legible, so guidance arises from ordered pursuit of the account rather than from isolated assertion.

#### Subchannel B. Death, deafness, sealing, and retreat close the auditory path
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A call is emitted, but loss of life, absent hearing, sealed openings, extinguished acoustic impact, and bodily retreat prevent reception.
- Active motifs: loss of hearing (quranic:root_000884:B001/m01); sealed opening (quranic:root_000884:B002/m01); disappearance of a sound's impact (quranic:root_000884:B006/m01); hearing by the ear (quranic:root_000741:B001/m01); causing another to hear (quranic:root_000741:B004/m01); loss of life-force (quranic:root_001454:B001/m01); stillness like sleep or decay (quranic:root_001454:B012/m01); vocal call (quranic:root_000478:B001/m01); turning away (quranic:root_001684:B007/m01); the back side (quranic:root_000458:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:80 `س م ع` (تُسْمِع), `م و ت` (الْمَوْتَى), `ص م م` (الصُّم), `د ع و` (الدُّعَاء), `و ل ي` (وَلَّوْا), and `د ب ر` (مُدْبِرِين).
- Synthesis: Failed hearing is assembled as a blocked circuit with several independent closures. The voice may be produced, but the receiver lacks animation, an open auditory passage, preserved acoustic impact, or bodily orientation toward the call.

#### Subchannel C. Hearing becomes guidance when assent and surrender remain possible
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Unlike the closed receiver, the believing hearer accepts the sign, is reoriented from blindness, and hands over resistance.
- Active motifs: understanding and compliance through hearing (quranic:root_000741:B003/m01); making another understand (quranic:root_000741:B004/m01); guidance toward a route (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01); loss of sight (quranic:root_001049:B001/m01); blindness of insight (quranic:root_001049:B002/m01); inward assent (quranic:root_000054:B002/m01); visible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01); surrender and handing over (quranic:root_000737:B012/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:81 `ه د ي` (بِهَادِي), `ع م ي` (الْعُمْي), `س م ع` (تُسْمِع), `ء م ن` (يُؤْمِن), `ء ي ي` (بِءَايَاتِنَا), and `س ل م` (مُسْلِمُون).
- Synthesis: Hearing here includes comprehension and enacted acceptance. Guidance does not force the blind route open; it reaches the receiver whose assent permits the sign to become understood and whose surrender completes the response.

#### Subchannel D. A hidden crawler emerges from earth and enters speech
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Slow, initially concealed motion rises out of the lower ground and becomes intelligible speech directed at people who lacked certainty about signs.
- Active motifs: crawling on earth (quranic:root_000457:B001/m01); hidden permeation (quranic:root_000457:B003/m01); emergence from confinement (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01); extraction from concealment (quranic:root_000400:B002/m01); lower ground (quranic:root_000025:B001/m01); intelligible exchange (quranic:root_001316:B001/m01); meaningful utterance (quranic:root_001316:B002/m01); visible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01); stable certainty (quranic:root_001696:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:82 `د ب ب` (دَابَّة), `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض), `خ ر ج` (أَخْرَجْنَا), `ك ل م` (تُكَلِّمُهُمْ), `ء ي ي` (بِءَايَاتِنَا), and `ي ق ن` (لَا يُوقِنُون).
- Synthesis: The speaking creature crosses two thresholds: concealed earthly movement becomes visible animal motion, then animal motion becomes meaningful address. The sign speaks precisely where human certainty had failed.

#### Subchannel E. Breath in a horn converts warning into unavoidable arrival
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Wind is sent into a horn, the blast spreads fear through upper and lower realms, and every creature is brought into compelled submission.
- Active motifs: wind blown into an object (quranic:root_001529:B001/m01); inflation by air (quranic:root_001529:B002/m01); horn of blowing (quranic:root_000891:B004/m01); terror (quranic:root_001152:B001/m01); flight toward a refuge (quranic:root_001152:B003/m01); upper realm (quranic:root_000745:B004/m01); lower realm (quranic:root_000025:B001/m01); unavoidable arrival (quranic:root_000009:B001/m01); coerced abasement (quranic:root_000463:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:87 `ن ف خ` (يُنفَخ), `ص و ر` (الصُّور), `ف ز ع` (فَزِع), `س م و` (السَّمَاوَات), `ء ر ض` (الْأَرْض), `ء ت ي` (ءَاتُوه), and `د خ ر` (دَاخِرِين).
- Synthesis: The trumpet is a breath-powered summons whose reception is universal rather than elective. Its acoustic event passes immediately into bodily fear, search for refuge, arrival, and abasement.

### 15. P5 (27:76-93) - Orientation Corrected by Actual Motion
- Semantic invariant: Bodies and landscapes are first read through apparent orientation or stillness, then corrected by a truer account of rest, movement, direction, or overturning.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:80-81, 27:86, and 27:88-90 juxtapose backs and guidance, night rest and day visibility, apparently fixed mountains in motion, and faces overturned.
- Surprising reach: Solidity is not the opposite of motion: a fixed-looking mountain can move like a cloud, while a human face can become the terminal surface of a moral trajectory.

#### Subchannel A. Night closes motion and day opens sight
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Darkness supplies a familiar enclosure in which motion ceases and the self settles; daylight opens the visual field for action.
- Active motifs: darkness and duration of night (quranic:root_001392:B001/m01); cessation of motion (quranic:root_000726:B001/m01); familiar place of rest (quranic:root_000726:B004/m01); day opening in light (quranic:root_001559:B002/m01); eyesight (quranic:root_000121:B001/m01); perceptible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:86 `ل ي ل` (اللَّيْل), `س ك ن` (لِيَسْكُنُوا), `ن ه ر` (النَّهَار), `ب ص ر` (مُبْصِرًا), and `ء ي ي` (ءَايَات).
- Synthesis: The day-night pair is organized by complementary capacities. Night is not merely dark but a settling medium; day is not merely time but an opening of perceptual range.

#### Subchannel B. Mountains appear fixed while passing like drawn cloud
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A massive solid form is visually estimated as motionless, yet it traverses space with the smooth extension of cloud under perfected workmanship.
- Active motifs: visual perception (quranic:root_000531:B001/m01); uncertain estimation (quranic:root_000318:B002/m01); elevated solid mass (quranic:root_000217:B001/m01); bedrock that stops excavation (quranic:root_000217:B005/m01); hard ground (quranic:root_000258:B004/m01); fixed boundary (quranic:root_000258:B008/m01); passage and traversal (quranic:root_001414:B001/m01); drawn extension (quranic:root_000680:B001/m01); moving cloud (quranic:root_000680:B002/m01); made work (quranic:root_000885:B001/m01); mastered construction (quranic:root_000184:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:88 `ر ء ي` (تَرَى), `ج ب ل` (الْجِبَال), `ح س ب` (تَحْسَبُهَا), `ج م د` (جَامِدَة), `م ر ر` (تَمُرُّ/مَرَّ), `س ح ب` (السَّحَاب), `ص ن ع` (صُنْع), and `ت ق ن` (أَتْقَن).
- Synthesis: The scene deliberately maximizes the conflict between appearance and process. Every lexical marker of hardness and fixed boundary intensifies the correction: apparent immobility is itself moving within a mastered larger order.

#### Subchannel C. Backs turn from guidance and faces are finally overturned
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Refusal begins as turning the receptive front away, develops into loss of direction, and ends with the face physically becoming the surface of forced descent.
