- Active motifs: course and bearing (quranic:root_001583:B002/m01); face and exposed front (quranic:root_001630:B001/m01); direction and destination (quranic:root_001630:B002/m01); blow to the face (quranic:root_001630:B013/m01); rear side (quranic:root_000458:B001/m01); turning away (quranic:root_001684:B007/m01); overturning onto the face (quranic:root_001278:B001/m01); tumbling into a depth (quranic:root_001278:B003/m01); moral badness (quranic:root_000755:B001/m01); burning fire (quranic:root_001564:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:80 `و ل ي` (وَلَّوْا) and `د ب ر` (مُدْبِرِين); 27:81 `ه د ي` (بِهَادِي); 27:90 `و ج ه` (وُجُوهُهُمْ), `ك ب ب` (كُبَّت), `س و ء` (السَّيِّئَة), and `ن و ر` (النَّار).
- Synthesis: Orientation carries moral consequence without collapsing into metaphor. Turning the front away from a guiding call establishes a trajectory whose terminal bodily image is the face itself overturned into fire.

### 16. P5 (27:76-93) - Judgment Returning Action to Its Actor
- Semantic invariant: Judgment gathers separated claims and persons, fixes their relation to knowledge and action, and returns good or bad consequences to the one who brought them.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:78 judges a dispute, 27:83-85 gathers and questions deniers, and 27:89-90 repays what each person brings.
- Surprising reach: The judicial process is spatial and acoustic: cohorts are driven and restrained, speech is elicited and then cut off, and deeds arrive like objects carried into court.

#### Subchannel A. A dispute is cut by an informed and effective ruling
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Opposed positions are placed before a judge whose knowledge identifies the right relation and whose ruling makes that relation effective.
- Active motifs: decisive judgment (quranic:root_001237:B001/m01); execution through perfected action (quranic:root_001237:B005/m01); adjudication between people (quranic:root_000348:B002/m01); knowledge that reaches the right (quranic:root_000348:B003/m01); binding precision (quranic:root_000348:B004/m01); middle relation between parties (quranic:root_000170:B002/m01); prevailing force (quranic:root_001008:B002/m01); disclosed knowledge (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:78 `ق ض ي` (يَقْضِي), `ب ي ن` (بَيْنَهُم), `ح ك م` (بِحُكْمِهِ), `ع ز ز` (الْعَزِيز), and `ع ل م` (الْعَلِيم).
- Synthesis: Judgment joins discernment to execution. Knowledge finds the correct relation between claims, while decisive and prevailing action prevents the ruling from remaining a merely advisory statement.

#### Subchannel B. Deniers are mustered, restrained, questioned, and silenced
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A cohort is driven from each community, held in order, brought forward for interrogation, confronted with incomplete knowledge, and finally deprived of speech when the sentence falls.
- Active motifs: gathering and driving to a destination (quranic:root_000324:B001/m01); successive cohort (quranic:root_001184:B001/m01); organized restraint (quranic:root_001644:B001/m01); arrival (quranic:root_000281:B001/m01); spoken interrogation (quranic:root_001272:B001/m01); false denial (quranic:root_001290:B001/m01); comprehensive knowledge (quranic:root_000372:B004/m01); disclosed knowledge (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01); sentence falling and becoming fixed (quranic:root_001675:B001/m01); severe event (quranic:root_001675:B002/m01); speech (quranic:root_001519:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:83 `ح ش ر` (نَحْشُر), `ف و ج` (فَوْجًا), `ك ذ ب` (يُكَذِّب), and `و ز ع` (يُوزَعُون); 27:84 `ج ي ء` (جَاءُوا), `ق و ل` (قَال), `ك ذ ب` (أَكَذَّبْتُم), `ح و ط` (تُحِيطُوا), and `ع ل م` (عِلْمًا); 27:85 `و ق ع` (وَقَع), `ق و ل` (الْقَوْل), and `ن ط ق` (يَنطِقُون).
- Synthesis: The court reverses the ordinary speech relation. Those who had spoken denial are assembled and questioned; once their lack of encompassing knowledge is exposed, the fixed sentence closes speech altogether.

#### Subchannel C. Good and bad arrive as objects that receive matching return
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Each person brings an enacted quality into judgment; beneficial action returns as greater good, while bad action returns as bodily overturning.
- Active motifs: bringing an object into presence (quranic:root_000281:B004/m01); desirable good (quranic:root_000323:B001/m01); enacted beneficence (quranic:root_000323:B002/m01); beneficial surplus (quranic:root_000452:B001/m01); moral badness (quranic:root_000755:B001/m01); matching recompense (quranic:root_000244:B001/m01); intentional action (quranic:root_001046:B001/m01); overturning onto the face (quranic:root_001278:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:89 `ج ي ء` (جَاء), `ح س ن` (الْحَسَنَة), and `خ ي ر` (خَيْر); 27:90 `ج ي ء` (جَاء), `س و ء` (السَّيِّئَة), `ك ب ب` (كُبَّت), `ج ز ي` (تُجْزَوْن), and `ع م ل` (تَعْمَلُون).
- Synthesis: The deed is treated as something carried by its actor, and judgment sends its quality back in commensurate form. Recompense therefore discloses rather than invents the relation between action and outcome.

### 17. P5 (27:76-93) - Entrustment, Sanctuary, and Self-Returning Guidance
- Semantic invariant: Security comes from placing agency under an adequate keeper, entering a protected order, and accepting guidance whose benefit returns to the accepting self.
- Surface relation: direct; 27:79 commands reliance, 27:91 joins worship to the protected city, and 27:92-93 returns guidance to the self and promises recognizable signs.
- Surprising reach: Reliance, sacred space, and recognition all preserve agency through right placement rather than passive withdrawal.

#### Subchannel A. A true cause is entrusted to a sufficient keeper
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person hands an affair to one capable of preserving and completing it, grounding reliance in a fixed correspondence with reality.
- Active motifs: handing an affair to another (quranic:root_001681:B001/m01); reliance (quranic:root_001681:B002/m01); adequate keeper (quranic:root_001681:B006/m01); truth fixed to reality (quranic:root_000347:B001/m01); binding entitlement (quranic:root_000347:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:79 `و ك ل` (فَتَوَكَّل), `ء ل ه` (اللَّه), `ح ق ق` (الْحَق), and `ب ي ن` (الْمُبِين).
- Synthesis: Entrustment is rational because the receiver is sufficient and the entrusted cause is true. Reliance transfers management without dissolving responsibility or reality.

#### Subchannel B. The delimited city is protected through prohibition and worship
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A bounded inhabited place is surrounded by inviolable rights; the speaker is commanded to worship its sovereign Lord and enter comprehensive surrender.
- Active motifs: binding command (quranic:root_000051:B002/m01); submissive worship (quranic:root_000973:B003/m01); sovereign lordship (quranic:root_000532:B001/m01); bounded land-place (quranic:root_000148:B001/m01); abiding in a city (quranic:root_000148:B009/m01); prohibition (quranic:root_000313:B001/m01); spatial sanctuary (quranic:root_000313:B003/m01); inviolable right (quranic:root_000313:B006/m01); comprehensive totality (quranic:root_001315:B003/m01); wholeness without injury (quranic:root_000737:B001/m01); surrender (quranic:root_000737:B012/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:91 `ء م ر` (أُمِرْتُ), `ع ب د` (أَعْبُد), `ر ب ب` (رَبَّ), `ب ل د` (الْبَلْدَة), `ح ر م` (حَرَّمَهَا), `ك ل ل` (كُلُّ), and `س ل م` (الْمُسْلِمِين).
- Synthesis: Sanctuary is constructed from place, prohibition, right, and allegiance. The city's security is not detached from worship; both locate persons and possessions within an order whose boundaries may not be violated.

#### Subchannel C. Guidance benefits its receiver and culminates in recognition
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Recited warning offers a route; accepting it benefits the self, refusing it leaves the path, and later displayed signs become recognizable while every action remains observed.
- Active motifs: guidance toward truth (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01); the self as beneficiary (quranic:root_001533:B012/m01); deviation from the route (quranic:root_000913:B001/m01); warning that awakens caution (quranic:root_001488:B001/m01); visible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01); making another see (quranic:root_000531:B012/m01); recognition by distinguishing marks (quranic:root_001002:B003/m01); inattention (quranic:root_001097:B001/m01); intentional action (quranic:root_001046:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:92 `ه د ي` (اهْتَدَى/يَهْتَدِي), `ن ف س` (لِنَفْسِهِ), `ض ل ل` (ضَلَّ), and `ن ذ ر` (الْمُنذِرِين); 27:93 `ء ي ي` (ءَايَاتِهِ), `ر ء ي` (سَيُرِيكُمْ), `ع ر ف` (فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا), `غ ف ل` (بِغَافِل), and `ع م ل` (تَعْمَلُون).
- Synthesis: Guidance is offered, not externally credited to the receiver's account. Its benefit returns to the self that follows it, while shown signs and observed actions ensure that neither recognition nor refusal disappears from view.

## Standalone Subchannels

### S1. P1 (27:10) - A Thrown Staff Becomes a Moving Serpent and Reverses the Viewer
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A handheld support is cast down, becomes an oscillating snake, and turns the observer from approach into fearful retreat before return is commanded.
- Active motifs: casting down (quranic:root_001372:B005/m01); staff (quranic:root_005713:B001/m01); visible oscillation (quranic:root_001588:B001/m01); snake (quranic:root_000266:B012/m01); sight (quranic:root_000531:B001/m01); anticipatory fear (quranic:root_000447:B001/m01); retreat (quranic:root_001684:B007/m01); return on the heel (quranic:root_001033:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:10 `ل ق ي` (أَلْقِ), `ع ص و` (عَصَاك), `ه ز ز` (تَهْتَز), `ج ن ن` (جَان), `ر ء ي` (رَءَاهَا), `خ و ف` (تَخَف/يَخَاف), `و ل ي` (وَلَّى), and `ع ق ب` (يُعَقِّب).
- Synthesis: The transformation reverses both object and observer. A tool associated with bodily support becomes autonomous animal motion, and seeing produces a backward trajectory that must itself be arrested.

### S2. P1 (27:11-14) - Wrong Is Replaced, Covered, and Read by Its Outcome
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A misplaced or withheld act is changed in state, replaced by beneficence, protected from punitive effect, and evaluated by what follows.
- Active motifs: withholding from a right (quranic:root_000967:B008/m01); one thing taking another's place (quranic:root_000095:B001/m01); change of state (quranic:root_000095:B002/m01); enacted good (quranic:root_000323:B002/m01); moral badness (quranic:root_000755:B001/m01); covering sin and protecting the wrongdoer (quranic:root_001096:B002/m01); mercy (quranic:root_000552:B001/m01); consequential endpoint (quranic:root_001033:B006/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:11 `ظ ل م` (ظَلَم), `ب د ل` (بَدَّل), `ح س ن` (حُسْنًا), `س و ء` (سُوء), `غ ف ر` (غَفُور), and `ر ح م` (رَحِيم); 27:14 `ظ ل م` (ظُلْمًا) and `ع ق ب` (عَاقِبَة).
- Synthesis: Repair is a process rather than a relabeling. The prior state is displaced by enacted good, forgiveness covers its punitive trace, and the eventual outcome reveals whether the transition was completed.

### S3. P1 (27:3-10) - A Latent Crop Comes Forth, Grows, Shakes, and Ripens
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Yield emerges, increases, moves with renewed plant life, approaches dryness while retaining green, and begins to ripen.
- Active motifs: crop yield coming forth (quranic:root_000009:B007/m01); vegetative increase (quranic:root_000637:B001/m01); vegetation shaking into life (quranic:root_001588:B002/m01); crop near dryness with residual green (quranic:root_000821:B005/m01); dates beginning to ripen (quranic:root_001684:B016/m01); abiding growth in good (quranic:root_000109:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:3 `ء ت ي` (يُؤْتُون) and `ز ك و` (الزَّكَاة); 27:7 `ء ت ي` (ءَاتِيكُم) and `ش ه ب` (شِهَاب); 27:8 `ب ر ك` (بُورِكَ); 27:10 `ه ز ز` (تَهْتَز) and `و ل ي` (وَلَّى).
- Synthesis: The lexical sequence forms a complete plant cycle distributed across the pericope. It gives the visible transformations a quiet organic counterimage: emergence and motion can be signs of life and maturation, not only abrupt miracle or threat.

### S4. P3 (27:46) - Haste Pulls Harm Ahead of Good
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Impatience reverses the intended temporal order by demanding distress before beneficence, while forgiveness and mercy offer a slower reparative sequence.
- Active motifs: premature advancement (quranic:root_000987:B001/m01); experienced harm (quranic:root_000755:B002/m01); desirable good (quranic:root_000323:B001/m01); enacted beneficence (quranic:root_000323:B002/m01); temporal precedence (quranic:root_001198:B002/m01); forgiveness protecting from consequence (quranic:root_001096:B002/m01); mercy (quranic:root_000552:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:46 `ع ج ل` (تَسْتَعْجِلُون), `س و ء` (بِالسَّيِّئَة), `ق ب ل` (قَبْل), `ح س ن` (الْحَسَنَة), `غ ف ر` (تَسْتَغْفِرُون), and `ر ح م` (تُرْحَمُون).
- Synthesis: The error is one of sequence as well as value. Haste drags the harmful term forward; repentance, forgiveness, and mercy restore an order in which repair precedes consequence.

### S5. P4 (27:60-66) - A Shaft Penetrates a Gap and Locks Materials Together
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A pointed wooden shaft enters a narrow interval, pierces material, and either wounds it or organizes separate pieces into one locked structure.
- Active motifs: shaft inserted through a gap (quranic:root_000435:B005/m01); penetrating and stringing with a point (quranic:root_000812:B002/m01); interlocked spears and thrusting (quranic:root_000777:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:60 `ش ج ر` (شَجَرَهَا); 27:61 `خ ل ل` (خِلَالَهَا); 27:66 `ش ك ك` (شَك).
- Synthesis: This latent mechanism pressures the pericope's benign channels and barriers with a counter-operation. An interval can conduct water, but it can also admit a piercing tool; joining can stabilize materials or become violent penetration.

### S6. P5 (27:78-88) - The World as Tightly Woven, Mastered Work
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Fibers are woven firmly, speech is made structurally sound, judgment is bound, and skilled workmanship produces a mastered whole.
- Active motifs: well-made weaving (quranic:root_000217:B007/m01); tightly woven cloth or speech (quranic:root_000347:B010/m01); binding precision (quranic:root_000348:B004/m01); mastery of work (quranic:root_000184:B001/m01); skilled handcraft (quranic:root_000885:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:78 `ح ك م` (بِحُكْمِهِ); 27:79 `ح ق ق` (الْحَق); 27:88 `ج ب ل` (الْجِبَال), `ت ق ن` (أَتْقَن), and `ص ن ع` (صُنْع).
- Synthesis: The craft scene joins legal, verbal, textile, and cosmic firmness without collapsing their operations. What looks like immovable mountain mass belongs to a larger fabric whose reliability lies in skilled construction, not in local stillness.

### S7. P5 (27:76-88) - The Earth-Creature Emerges Through a Latent Birth Sequence
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A containing womb gathers a fetus, pregnancy becomes externally visible, issue comes forth, and the new creature begins moving on the ground.
- Active motifs: womb containing a fetus (quranic:root_001210:B004/m01); visible pregnancy (quranic:root_000531:B010/m01); pregnancy becoming apparent (quranic:root_001232:B008/m01); yield or offspring coming forth (quranic:root_000009:B007/m01); extraction from concealment (quranic:root_000400:B002/m01); crawling creature (quranic:root_000457:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:76,92 `ق ر ء` (الْقُرْءَان); 27:76 `ق ص ص` (يَقُص); 27:82 `خ ر ج` (أَخْرَجْنَا) and `د ب ب` (دَابَّة); 27:86,88 `ر ء ي` (يَرَوْا/تَرَى); 27:87 `ء ت ي` (ءَاتُوه).
- Synthesis: The distributed reproductive senses form a coherent emergence sequence that materializes the earth bringing forth a speaking creature. The scene does not identify the earth literally as a womb; it supplies a latent model of containment, visible term, issue, and first movement.

### S8. Whole-surah - A Well-Head, Wheel, Rope, and Bucket Route Water
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A timbered well-mouth supports a lifting wheel; a twisted drawing rope carries a handled bucket upward, and the raised water is directed into a channel.
- Active motifs: timbered well-head and watering platform (quranic:root_001000:B004/m01); well-wheel for raising water (quranic:root_000373:B016/m01); long tightly twisted bucket-rope (quranic:root_000796:B002/m01); single-loop water bucket (quranic:root_000737:B011/m01); bucket handle or crosspiece that balances the load (quranic:root_000741:B008/m01); watercourse directed toward a basin (quranic:root_000009:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:23,26,38,41-42 `ع ر ش` (عَرْش); 27:8 `ح و ل` (حَوْل); 27:24 `ش ط ن` (الشَّيْطَان); 27:31,38,42,44,59,81,91 `س ل م` (مُسْلِمِين/أَسْلَم/سَلَام/مُسْلِمُون); 27:80-81 `س م ع` (تُسْمِع); `ء ت ي` recurs from 27:3 through 27:87; the primary water-and-garden frame is 27:60-64.
- Synthesis: This apparatus materializes the water-and-garden argument of 27:60-64. Human agents can frame a well, raise and balance a bucket, and cut a channel, but every operation begins after water is available; the scene therefore supports the distinction between managing provision and causing the garden's trees to grow.

### S9. Whole-surah - Pole, Rudder, and Mooring Turn Sea Guidance Into Practice
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A sailor moves a vessel with a pushing pole, corrects and steadies it with its steering apparatus, and ends the passage by holding it at a mooring.
- Active motifs: pushing a ship with a sailor's pole (quranic:root_001413:B006/m01); rudder or stern-piece that steadies a ship (quranic:root_000726:B008/m01); ship coming to rest at its mooring or anchor (quranic:root_000564:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:44 `م ر د` (مُمَرَّد); 27:18,86 `س ك ن` (مَسَاكِنَكُمْ/يَسْكُنُوا); 27:61 `ر س و` (رَوَاسِي); the primary sea-guidance anchor is 27:63 `ه د ي` (يَهْدِيكُمْ) and `ب ح ر` (الْبَحْر).
- Synthesis: The handling sequence materializes sea guidance in 27:63 as repeated directed correction rather than abstract orientation. Poling initiates motion, steering contains drift, and mooring converts a bearing into stable arrival.

### S10. Whole-surah - Ink, Lines, Heading, and Signature Give Speech a Durable Body
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A deft hand takes ink from an inkwell with a pen, forms ordered lines, adds a heading, completes a written document, and leaves an authenticating mark.
- Active motifs: skilled work with nimble fingers (quranic:root_001556:B011/m01); inkwell supplying ink to a pen (quranic:root_001407:B005/m01); written rows fixed in a book (quranic:root_000704:B001/m01); heading or title added to a document (quranic:root_001041:B002/m01); written document in the ant-root lexicon (quranic:root_001556:B010/m01); signature and residual trace of writing (quranic:root_001675:B011/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:18 `ن م ل` (النَّمْل/نَمْلَة); 27:36 `م د د` (تُمِدُّونَنِ); 27:68 `س ط ر` (أَسَاطِير); 27:25,74 `ع ل ن` (تُعْلِنُون/يُعْلِنُون); 27:82,85 `و ق ع` (وَقَع); the primary written-object anchors are 27:1,28-29,75 `ك ت ب` (كِتَاب/كِتَابِي).
- Synthesis: The workshop materializes the Quranic book, Solomon's letter, and the clarifying record as produced and durable objects rather than disembodied messages. The ant root supplies both dexterous fingers and a written document, supporting the surah's wider claim that small-scale agency can carry consequential speech while heading and signature make that speech publicly attributable.

### S11. Whole-surah - The Pupil Receives an Image From a Mirror-Clear Surface
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A viewer fixes the gaze on a clear reflective surface; the surface presents an appearance, and a miniature human image is received in the black of the eye.
- Active motifs: human image visible in the pupil (quranic:root_000059:B005/m01); fixed and intense gaze (quranic:root_000300:B004/m01); mirror as a viewed appearance (quranic:root_000531:B006/m01); crystal-clear mirror likened to water (quranic:root_001458:B007/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:7,17,56 `ء ن س` (ءَانَسْتُ/الْإِنس/أُنَاس); 27:60 `ح د ق` (حَدَائِق); 27:10,20,40,44,86,88,93 `ر ء ي` (رَءَاهَا/أَرَى/رَءَاهُ/رَأَتْهُ/يَرَوْا/تَرَى/سَيُرِيكُمْ); 27:60 `م و ه` (مَاء).
- Synthesis: This optical scene materializes the throne-recognition test and the glass-floor error in 27:40-44. Sight receives constructed images through eye and surface, so exceptional clarity does not guarantee correct identification; recognition still requires testing, bodily response, and verbal correction.

### S12. Whole-surah - A Bird Moves From Quarry to Knowledge-Bearing Witness
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A hunter goes out, sets a fowling snare, checks whether struck quarry has died, and can complete the taking of life by cutting the throat.
- Active motifs: departure in pursuit of game (quranic:root_000745:B006/m01); hunter's snare set for birds (quranic:root_000791:B006/m01); checking whether wounded quarry is dead (quranic:root_001454:B014/m01); slaughter by cutting the throat (quranic:root_000508:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:25,30,60,64-65,75,87 `س م و` (السَّمَاوَات/اسْم/السَّمَاء); 27:59,63 `ش ر ك` (يُشْرِكُون); 27:80 `م و ت` (الْمَوْتَى); 27:21 `ذ ب ح` (لَأَذْبَحَنَّهُ); the primary bird inquiry and report occupy 27:20-22.
- Synthesis: The hunting scene usefully pressures the hoopoe episode. A bird first appears available to sovereign capture and slaughter, but the absent creature returns as a witness with a comprehensive, certain report; knowledge-bearing speech suspends the ordinary reduction of the bird to quarry.

### S13. Whole-surah - Gaming Lots Mark a Fifth Position and a Losing Stake
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Gaming arrows are kept together in a hide or container; one marked lot occupies the fifth position, while a losing lot identifies the failed participant and what gambling takes away.
- Active motifs: hide container holding the arrows of maysir (quranic:root_000532:B010/m01); fifth gaming lot (quranic:root_001533:B016/m01); losing lot and the stake lost through gambling (quranic:root_000458:B019/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:8,19,26,40,44,73-74,78,91,93 `ر ب ب` (رَبّ); 27:14,40,44,92 `ن ف س` (أَنفُس/نَفْس); 27:10,80 `د ب ر` (مُدْبِرًا/مُدْبِرِينَ); the primary truth tests and recompense scenes are 27:27,40-42,89-90.
- Synthesis: The lot game usefully pressures the surah's repeated testing and judgment. A concealed draw divides gain from loss by chance, whereas the hoopoe's report is verified, the throne is altered to test recognition, and deeds return according to their disclosed quality; the primary reading therefore presents judgment as evidentiary rather than random allocation.

### S14. Whole-surah - Shrouding and Interment Make the Grave a House
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: The dead person is covered and hidden, placed into a grave, and assigned a bounded resting place understood as a house.
- Active motifs: concealing the dead with shroud and grave (quranic:root_000266:B009/m01); interment that makes a person absent in the grave (quranic:root_001117:B009/m01); grave treated as the dead person's house (quranic:root_000166:B007/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:10,17,39 `ج ن ن` (جَانّ/الْجِنّ); 27:20,65,75 `غ ي ب` (الْغَائِبِين/الْغَيْب/غَائِبَة); 27:49,52 `ب ي ت` (لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ/بُيُوتُهُمْ); the primary death-and-emergence anchors are 27:67 and 27:80.
- Synthesis: Burial materializes the denial of emergence in 27:67 and the address to the dead in 27:80. Its operations are concealment, relocation, and bounded dwelling rather than annihilation, so the scene supports the primary pressure against treating the body's disappearance from view as a terminal account of it.

### S15. Whole-surah - Consecration, Standing, Offering, and Sacrifice Enact Sanctuary
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A worshipper enters a restricted consecrated state, stands at a named ritual station, conveys an offering to the sanctuary, and encounters the implements and places of sacrifice and prostration.
- Active motifs: entering consecration for pilgrimage (quranic:root_000313:B004/m01); standing at Arafat (quranic:root_001002:B007/m01); offering conveyed to the sanctuary (quranic:root_001583:B005/m01); knife, slaughter-place, and sacrificial station (quranic:root_000508:B003/m01); communal place of prostration (quranic:root_000675:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:91 `ح ر م` (حَرَّمَهَا); 27:93 `ع ر ف` (تَعْرِفُونَهَا); 27:2,24,35-36,41,63,77,81,92 `ه د ي` (هُدًى/يَهْتَدُون/هَدِيَّة/يَهْدِي/هَادِي/اهْتَدَى); 27:21 `ذ ب ح` (لَأَذْبَحَنَّهُ); 27:24-25 `س ج د` (يَسْجُدُون/يَسْجُدُوا).
- Synthesis: The rite materializes 27:91's protected city and commanded worship as embodied restriction, station, offering, sacrificial implement, and prayer place. It also reframes slaughter: the hoopoe faces a punitive threat in 27:21, whereas sacrificial killing is bounded by consecration, destination, and ritual purpose.

### S16. Whole-surah - Contract, Dower, Bridal Conveyance, and Household Form a Marriage Transfer
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A marriage is contracted, a dower accompanies it, the bride is conveyed to her spouse, and entry establishes a new household.
- Active motifs: marriage contract (quranic:root_001444:B004/m01); bridal dower (quranic:root_000852:B007/m01); bride conveyed to her husband (quranic:root_001583:B006/m01); marriage-house established upon entry (quranic:root_000166:B010/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:23,34 `م ل ك` (تَمْلِكُهُمْ/الْمُلُوك); 27:27,49,64,71 `ص د ق` (أَصَدَقْتَ/صَادِقُون); 27:2,24,35-36,41,63,77,81,92 `ه د ي` (هُدًى/هَدِيَّة/تَهْتَدِي/يَهْدِي/اهْتَدَى); 27:49,52 `ب ي ت` (لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ/بُيُوتُهُمْ); the primary palace declaration is 27:44.
- Synthesis: This social frame usefully pressures the Queen's palace climax. Royal ownership, a truth test, a conveyed gift, and entry into built space make transfer and possession a plausible latent script, but 27:44 resolves her relation as surrender with Solomon to the Lord of the worlds, not acquisition by Solomon; the marriage scene thus sharpens the stated object of submission.

### S17. Whole-surah - A Horse Race Measures Leader, Second Place, and Finish
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Horses run in competition; a leader gains the forward position, the second horse follows with its head at the leader's rear, and the winner reaches the marked end first.
- Active motifs: horses racing at rain-like speed (quranic:root_001431:B006/m01); second horse following immediately behind the leader (quranic:root_000880:B007/m01); leading horse that overcomes the field (quranic:root_000104:B008/m01); racer reaching and taking the finish (quranic:root_001684:B012/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:58 `م ط ر` (أَمْطَرْنَا/مَطَرًا/مَطَرُ); 27:7 `ص ل ي` (تَصْطَلُون); 27:63 `ب ر ر` (الْبَرّ); 27:10,28,49,80 `و ل ي` (وَلَّى/تَوَلَّ/وَلِيّه/وَلَّوْا); the primary competing transport claims occupy 27:38-40.
- Synthesis: The race scene reframes 27:38-40's competing time claims as measured precedence. Yet the surah refuses to let first arrival establish merit by itself: Solomon reads the settled throne as grace and a test of gratitude, so speed becomes an outcome to interpret rather than self-validating supremacy.

### S18. Whole-surah - A Blacksmith Sharpens a Blade on Anvil and Stone
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A blacksmith supports the work on an anvil, brings an iron edge against stone, and produces a long, keen blade or point ready for use.
- Active motifs: blacksmith as named craft worker (quranic:root_001596:B007/m01); anvil or raised working stone (quranic:root_001042:B009/m01); sharpening iron, knife, or sword on stone (quranic:root_001675:B009/m01); keen blade or weapon-point (quranic:root_000732:B006/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:49 `ه ل ك` (مَهْلِك); 27:14,31,63 `ع ل و` (عُلُوًّا/تَعْلُوا/تَعَالَى); 27:82,85 `و ق ع` (وَقَع); 27:21 `س ل ط` (سُلْطَان); the primary military-force frame is 27:33-37.
- Synthesis: The forge materializes the force claimed in 27:33 and threatened in 27:37 as prepared and maintained technology. Because a weapon's edge must be made, martial capacity remains instrumental rather than sovereign in itself; the surah places counsel, letter, evidence, and recognition before force.

### S19. P1 -> P5 - Quran Received Becomes Quran Recited
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: The Quran first moves toward a recipient as learned speech, then moves outward from that recipient as public recitation and instruction.
- Active motifs: received and learned speech (quranic:root_001372:B011/m01); recitation and instruction (quranic:root_001210:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:6 `ل ق ي` (تُلَقَّى) and `ق ر ء` (الْقُرْآن); P5 27:92 `ق ر ء` (أَتْلُوَ الْقُرْآن).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P5; causal role progression): the receiver at the opening becomes the reciter at the close. This supports the surah's primary framing of revelation as an entrusted transmission whose completed reception issues in instruction rather than private possession.

### S20. P1 -> P2 - Adorned Deeds Produce Blocked Movement
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The same act of making deeds look attractive first produces directionless wandering, then reappears with an explicit agent, blocked path, and failed guidance.
- Active motifs: cosmetic enhancement (quranic:root_000660:B002/m01); intentional deeds (quranic:root_001046:B001/m01); confused wandering without direction (quranic:root_001048:B001/m01); turning and blocking (quranic:root_000848:B001/m01); traversable path (quranic:root_000672:B001/m01); guidance toward truth (quranic:root_001583:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:4 `ز ي ن` (زَيَّنَّا), `ع م ل` (أَعْمَالَهُمْ), and `ع م ه` (يَعْمَهُون); P2 27:24 `ز ي ن` (زَيَّنَ), `ع م ل` (أَعْمَالَهُمْ), `ص د د` (فَصَدَّهُمْ), `س ب ل` (السَّبِيل), and `ه د ي` (يَهْتَدُون).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P2; repeated causal signature): P1 states the mechanism, and P2 materializes it in the sun-worship scene. The recurrence supports a primary reading in which error persists not for lack of a path but because beautified action changes how agents evaluate and traverse it.

### S21. P1 -> P5 - Sought Fire Reverses Into Received Fire
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A traveler initially approaches fire to obtain warmth and news; at judgment, the bearer of a bad deed is instead driven face-first into fire.
- Active motifs: burning fire (quranic:root_001564:B002/m01); ember taken from its source (quranic:root_001196:B001/m01); news and inward knowledge (quranic:root_000387:B001/m01); moral badness (quranic:root_000755:B001/m01); overturning onto the face (quranic:root_001278:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:7-8 `ن و ر` (نَارًا/النَّار), 27:7 `ق ب س` (قَبَس) and `خ ب ر` (خَبَر); P5 27:90 `ن و ر` (النَّار), `س و ء` (بِالسَّيِّئَة), and `ك ب ب` (كُبَّتْ).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P5; object-role reversal): fire changes from a sought source of practical benefit that opens revelation into a destination imposed by recompense. The reversal usefully pressures a one-note reading of the object: orientation, action, and response determine whether approach to fire becomes disclosure or punishment.

### S22. P1 -> P3 - Nine Signs Are Answered by Nine Corrupters
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: The same exact count first delimits a body of divine signs, then delimits a close male band whose coordinated action opposes reform.
- Active motifs: number nine (quranic:root_000181:B001/m01); visible sign (quranic:root_000074:B003/m01); close male band (quranic:root_000605:B001/m01); action departing from sound order into corruption (quranic:root_001154:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:12 `ت س ع` (تِسْعِ) and `ء ي ي` (آيَات); P3 27:48 `ت س ع` (تِسْعَة), `ر ه ط` (رَهْط), and `ف س د` (يُفْسِدُون).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P3; counted-role reversal): nine marks authorized evidence in P1 and compact counter-agency in P3. The repeated count sharpens the primary conflict by setting a bounded company of corrupters against a bounded body of signs rather than treating "nine" as incidental enumeration.

### S23. P1 -> P3 -> P4 - Action Is Read at Its Outcome
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A repeated command directs the observer past present claims to the consequential endpoint left by corruption, plotting, and crime.
- Active motifs: directed sight and intellectual inspection (quranic:root_001520:B001/m01); action-generated endpoint (quranic:root_001033:B006/m01); corruption as departure from sound order (quranic:root_001154:B001/m01); crime and culpability (quranic:root_000239:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:14 `ن ظ ر` (فَانظُرْ) and `ع ق ب` (عَاقِبَةُ); P3 27:51 repeats `فَانظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ`; P4 27:69 repeats `فَانظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ` after `سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْض`.
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P3 -> P4; repeated scene signature and causal sequence): denial is first judged by its endpoint, the Thamud plot supplies a narrated instance, and travel turns prior endpoints into inspectable evidence. This supports the primary reading by making historical consequence a public trace that tests claims after speech and intention have become inaccessible.

### S24. P1 -> P3 -> P4 -> P5 - The Call-Response Circuit Reverses Direction and Outcome
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Divine address arrests a retreating messenger; a corrupt community answers prophetic correction with expulsion; God answers a distressed caller with relief; final deniers retreat beyond effective hearing.
- Active motifs: raised call (quranic:root_001486:B002/m01); turning away (quranic:root_001684:B007/m01); rearward orientation (quranic:root_000458:B001/m01); responsive answer (quranic:root_000273:B003/m01); forced emergence from a place (quranic:root_000400:B001/m01); vocal appeal (quranic:root_000478:B001/m01); uncovering distress (quranic:root_001302:B001/m01); understanding and compliance through hearing (quranic:root_000741:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:8 `ن د و` (نُودِيَ) and 27:10 `و ل ي`/`د ب ر` (وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا); P3 27:56 `ج و ب` (جَوَابَ) and `خ ر ج` (أَخْرِجُوا); P4 27:62 `ج و ب` (يُجِيبُ), `د ع و` (دَعَاهُ), and `ك ش ف` (يَكْشِفُ); P5 27:80 `س م ع` (تُسْمِعُ), `د ع و` (الدُّعَاء), and `و ل ي`/`د ب ر` (وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P3 -> P4 -> P5; repeated discourse signature with role and outcome reversal): successful divine-human address runs in both directions, while resistant communities answer by removal or make themselves unreachable. The sequence reframes responsiveness as enacted orientation: hearing is demonstrated by return and relief, whereas refusal takes spatial form as expulsion or a turned back.

### S25. P1 -> P4 - Verbal Good News Becomes an Atmospheric Advance Sign
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A beneficial event is announced before arrival, first through Quranic good news and then through winds whose onset precedes mercy.
- Active motifs: good news that opens visible joy (quranic:root_000120:B005/m01); first signs and heralds (quranic:root_000120:B007/m01); recitation and instruction (quranic:root_001210:B002/m01); moving wind (quranic:root_000609:B003/m01); mercy and beneficence (quranic:root_000552:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P1 27:1-2 `ق ر ء` (الْقُرْآن), `ب ش ر` (بُشْرَى), and `ه د ي` (هُدًى); P4 27:63 `ر و ح` (الرِّيَاح), `ب ش ر` (بُشْرًا), and `ر ح م` (رَحْمَتِهِ).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P1 -> P4; shared functional invariant across media): verbal tidings and atmospheric heralds share the operation of making a coming benefit readable in advance. The wind materializes the primary description of revelation as good news: both orient a receiver toward mercy before the promised good is fully present.

### S26. P2 -> P5 - The Royal Muster Returns as a Court of Complete Knowledge
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Two sovereign scenes repeat the sequence of gathering cohorts, holding them in order, and testing claims about knowledge; the final court extends that sequence into a fixed verdict.
- Active motifs: gathering and driving to a destination (quranic:root_000324:B001/m01); organized restraint (quranic:root_001644:B001/m01); comprehensive informational enclosure (quranic:root_000372:B004/m01); truthful correspondence (quranic:root_000852:B001/m01); false denial (quranic:root_001290:B001/m01); sentence falling and becoming fixed (quranic:root_001675:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P2 27:17 `ح ش ر` (حُشِرَ) and `و ز ع` (يُوزَعُون), 27:22 `ح و ط` (أَحَطتُ), and 27:27 `ص د ق`/`ك ذ ب` (أَصَدَقْتَ/الْكَاذِبِينَ); P5 27:83 `ح ش ر` (نَحْشُرُ) and `و ز ع` (يُوزَعُون), 27:84 `ح و ط` (تُحِيطُوا) and `ك ذ ب` (أَكَذَّبْتُم), and 27:85 `و ق ع` (وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P2 -> P5; repeated court signature and epistemic role reversal): Solomon must test knowledge arriving from a subordinate, whereas the final court tests subordinates who denied without encompassing knowledge. The recurrence materializes judgment through an earlier royal procedure while sharply limiting the analogy: earthly sovereignty receives missing information, but divine judgment exposes its absence in others.

### S27. P2 -> P5 - Two False Estimates Reverse Solidity and Motion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The same perception-and-estimation sequence first treats a fixed transparent structure as liquid, then treats moving solid mountains as fixed.
- Active motifs: visual perception (quranic:root_000531:B001/m01); non-certain estimation (quranic:root_000318:B002/m01); polished smooth surface (quranic:root_001413:B002/m01); fragile transparent glass (quranic:root_001215:B012/m01); elevated solid mass (quranic:root_000217:B001/m01); passage and traversal (quranic:root_001414:B001/m01); moving cloud (quranic:root_000680:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P2 27:44 `ر ء ي`/`ح س ب` (رَأَتْهُ/حَسِبَتْهُ), `م ر د` (مُمَرَّد), and `ق ر ر` (قَوَارِيرَ); P5 27:88 `ر ء ي`/`ح س ب` (تَرَى/تَحْسَبُهَا), `ج ب ل` (الْجِبَال), `م ر ر` (تَمُرُّ), and `س ح ب` (السَّحَاب).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P2 -> P5; repeated visual signature and material-motion reversal): transparency makes solidity look fluid, while scale makes motion look fixed. The paired errors support the primary warning that sight supplies real appearances but estimation can still misassign material or movement until speech, event, or a larger frame corrects it.

### S28. P2 -> P5 - Creatures Gain Speech as Deniers Lose It
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Nonhuman utterance moves from bird-language, ant warning, and avian report to an earth-creature's address, while judged human deniers become unable to speak.
- Active motifs: intelligible speech shared by humans and animals (quranic:root_001519:B001/m01); meaningful public utterance (quranic:root_001272:B001/m01); intelligible exchange (quranic:root_001316:B001/m01); meaningful word or expression (quranic:root_001316:B002/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P2 27:16 `ن ط ق` (مَنطِقَ الطَّيْر), 27:18 `ق و ل` (قَالَتْ نَمْلَة), and 27:22 `ق و ل` (فَقَالَ); P5 27:82 `ك ل م` (تُكَلِّمُهُمْ) and 27:85 `ن ط ق` (لَا يَنطِقُون).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P2 -> P5; speaker-role reversal): creatures repeatedly carry intelligible warning or testimony, culminating in a creature addressing people just before deniers lose articulation. This reframes speech in the primary reading as granted communicative capacity answerable to truth, not an exclusively human possession that guarantees a truthful response.

### S29. P2 -> P4 - Gratitude Moves From Prayer and Trial to Collective Contrast
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A ruler asks to be inwardly prompted toward gratitude, interprets settled power as a gratitude test, and is later set against a majority that receives divine favor without thanking.
- Active motifs: inward prompting toward gratitude (quranic:root_001644:B002/m01); grateful recognition (quranic:root_000810:B001/m01); unowed favor (quranic:root_001163:B003/m01); trial that reveals quality (quranic:root_000153:B002/m01); the self as acting beneficiary (quranic:root_001533:B012/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P2 27:19 `و ز ع` (أَوْزِعْنِي) and `ش ك ر` (أَشْكُرَ), and 27:40 `ف ض ل` (فَضْلِ), `ب ل و` (لِيَبْلُوَنِي), `ش ك ر` (أَشْكُرُ/شَكَرَ), and `ن ف س` (لِنَفْسِهِ); P4 27:73 `ف ض ل` (فَضْلٍ) and `ش ك ر` (لَا يَشْكُرُون).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P2 -> P4; role progression and collective contrast): gratitude begins as requested inward governance, becomes the interpretation of power under trial, and then exposes the majority's contrary response to favor. This supports the primary reading by making gratitude an enabled discipline whose benefit returns to the grateful actor, not payment needed by the giver.

### S30. P3 -> P4 - The Same Haste Pulls Harm Forward and Denies an Approaching Promise
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Impatient demand first attempts to place harm before good, then treats a promised event as absent even while part of it follows close behind.
- Active motifs: premature advancement (quranic:root_000987:B001/m01); experienced harm (quranic:root_000755:B002/m01); desirable good (quranic:root_000323:B001/m01); promise opening expectation (quranic:root_001662:B001/m01); following closely after (quranic:root_000556:B001/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P3 27:46 `ع ج ل` (تَسْتَعْجِلُون), `س و ء` (بِالسَّيِّئَة), and `ح س ن` (الْحَسَنَة); P4 27:71-72 `و ع د` (الْوَعْد), `ر د ف` (رَدِفَ), and the repeated `ع ج ل` (تَسْتَعْجِلُون).
- Synthesis: Bridge (P3 -> P4; repeated temporal operation and causal correction): both scenes compress an ordered future into an impatient present, but P4 answers by placing the demanded event immediately behind the demander. The recurrence reframes delay in the primary reading as sequence rather than absence and makes haste an error about temporal position.

### S31. P3 -> P4 - Descending Water Reverses From Punishment to Provision
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Water descends from above onto a receiving population or ground; the direction and material remain stable while the function reverses from destructive exposure to life-giving provision.
- Active motifs: falling rainwater (quranic:root_001431:B001/m01); rain specified as punishment (quranic:root_001431:B002/m01); exposure to what descends (quranic:root_001431:B003/m01); downward descent (quranic:root_001492:B001/m01); caused delivery from above (quranic:root_001492:B002/m01); water substance (quranic:root_001458:B001/m01); rain as provision (quranic:root_000560:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: P3 27:58 `م ط ر` (أَمْطَرْنَا/مَطَرًا/مَطَرُ), `س و ء` (فَسَاءَ), and `ن ذ ر` (الْمُنذَرِينَ); P4 27:60 `ن ز ل` (أَنزَلَ), `س م و` (السَّمَاءِ), and `م و ه` (مَاءً), with 27:64 `ر ز ق` (يَرْزُقُكُم) naming provision from above.
- Synthesis: Bridge (P3 -> P4; shared role map with outcome reversal): source, downward transfer, water, and receiver persist while purpose and result invert. The contrast supports the primary reading by locating the difference not in the material itself but in divine ordering: one descent removes a warned community, and the next sustains fertile life.

### S32. Whole-surah - A Levy Leaves the Payer and Enters Revenue
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A person or polity is assessed a financial obligation; money or yield is remitted from the payer and enters the receiver's estate as income.
- Active motifs: tribute remitted by a person or polity (quranic:root_000009:B008/m01); assessed poll or land payment (quranic:root_000244:B004/m01); money or yield paid under a specified obligation (quranic:root_000400:B003/m01); proceeds entering an estate as income (quranic:root_000464:B006/m01).
- Ayah anchors: `ء ت ي` recurs from 27:3 through 27:87, including 27:36-40 (ءَاتَىٰ/نَأْتِيَ/يَأْتِي/ءَاتِي); 27:90 `ج ز ي` (تُجْزَوْنَ); 27:12,25,37,56,67,82 `خ ر ج` (تَخْرُجْ/يُخْرِجُ/نُخْرِجَ/أَخْرِجُوا/مُخْرَجُونَ/أَخْرَجْنَا); 27:12,18-19,34,44 `د خ ل` (أَدْخِلْ/ادْخُلُوا/دَخَلُوا/ادْخُلِي); the primary diplomatic-gift frame is 27:35-37.
- Synthesis: This fiscal transfer materializes what the Queen's gift could have become: value exits one polity and is entered as another ruler's revenue. Solomon's answer refuses that settlement by returning the payment and locating his sufficiency in what God has given him, so the primary scene does not reduce allegiance or threatened conflict to a collectible levy.

### S33. Whole-surah - Fire and Weight Expose Plated Gold
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An assayer heats a metal presented as gold, exposes gilding over a different material, weighs a coin against known standards, and rejects the counterfeit.
- Active motifs: gold as the tested metal (quranic:root_000522:B001/m01); fire assay distinguishing sound from base metal (quranic:root_001128:B001/m01); gilding that makes a metal appear unlike its reality (quranic:root_001458:B005/m01); known ounce weight (quranic:root_001677:B004/m01); evenly weighted dinar (quranic:root_001273:B015/m01); rejection of counterfeit coin or error (quranic:root_000555:B003/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:28 `ذ ه ب` (اذْهَب); 27:47 `ف ت ن` (تُفْتَنُون); 27:60 `م و ه` (مَاءً); 27:53 `و ق ي` (يَتَّقُون); 27:39 `ق و م` (تَقُومَ/مَقَامِكَ); 27:40 `ر د د` (يَرْتَدَّ); the primary testing scenes are 27:27 and 27:40-44.
- Synthesis: Assay makes the surah's tests materially exact. Heat corrects a plated surface and weight corrects a declared value, just as the hoopoe's report, the altered throne, and the apparent water require operations that distinguish claim or appearance from composition and truth.

### S34. Whole-surah - Folded Cloth Is Cut and Fitted Into a Garment
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A cloth-folder makes the first fold in marked fabric, then the material is cut, stitched, and fitted into a finished garment.
- Active motifs: first folding of cloth (quranic:root_001226:B007/m01); cutting, stitching, and fitting cloth as a garment (quranic:root_001240:B012/m01); striped or line-marked fabric (quranic:root_000769:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:49 `ق س م` (تَقَاسَمُوا); 27:32 `ق ط ع` (قَاطِعَةً); 27:69 `س ي ر` (سِيرُوا); the primary garment-opening frame is 27:12 `ج ي ب` (جَيْبِكَ).
- Synthesis: Tailoring materializes the shirt opening in 27:12 as a deliberately formed boundary within a made object. The hand's controlled entry and luminous exit occur through ordinary folded and fitted cloth, sharpening the sign's sequence of enclosure, passage, and disclosure.

### S35. Whole-surah - A Fighter Dons a Helmet, Fitted Arms, and Shield
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A combatant puts on an iron helmet, is enclosed by tightly fitted defensive equipment, and carries a shield that interposes protection against attack.
- Active motifs: iron war helmet (quranic:root_000168:B004/m01); weaponry fitted tightly around its wearer (quranic:root_000812:B003/m01); protective shield or defensive weapon (quranic:root_000266:B008/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:12 `ب ي ض` (بَيْضَاء); 27:66 `ش ك ك` (شَكٍّ); 27:10,17,39 `ج ن ن` (جَانٌّ/الْجِنِّ); the primary host-and-force frame is 27:17 and 27:33-37.
- Synthesis: The arming scene materializes the severe force claimed by the Queen's council and threatened by Solomon as equipment borne by vulnerable bodies. Helmet, fitted arms, and shield make martial power prepared and defensive as well as destructive, supporting the surah's placement of command, counsel, and evidentiary testing around its use.

### S36. Whole-surah - A Night Observer Tracks Lunar Stations in Sequence
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An observer locates named lunar stations, identifies one position between the Pleiades and Aldebaran, watches Aldebaran follow the Pleiades, and reads successive lights as markers of time.
- Active motifs: the Balda lunar station and empty celestial place (quranic:root_000148:B004/m01); the Diqa station between or adjoining the Pleiades and Aldebaran (quranic:root_000925:B004/m01); Aldebaran following the Pleiades (quranic:root_000458:B013/m01); a star serving as a witness to time or state (quranic:root_000822:B008/m01); successive stars, night, and day following one another (quranic:root_000556:B005/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:91 `ب ل د` (الْبَلْدَةِ); 27:70 `ض ي ق` (ضَيْقٍ); 27:10,80 `د ب ر` (مُدْبِرًا/مُدْبِرِينَ); 27:32,49 `ش ه د` (تَشْهَدُون/شَهِدْنَا); 27:72 `ر د ف` (رَدِفَ); the primary darkness, night, and large-scale motion frames are 27:63,86,88.
- Synthesis: This is an observational procedure rather than a star catalog: relative position and recurrence make direction and time legible across successive views. It materializes guidance through land and sea darkness in 27:63 and supports the later correction of apparent stillness in 27:88, where large motion likewise exceeds a single glance.

### S37. Whole-surah - A Written Installment Contract Ends Enslaved Labor
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An enslaved worker and owner fix written terms; specified work, wages, and staged payments satisfy the agreement and culminate in release.
- Active motifs: enslavement that reduces a person to compelled labor (quranic:root_000973:B004/m01); written manumission contract with installment payments leading to freedom (quranic:root_001283:B005/m01); agreement fixing specified work or wages (quranic:root_001240:B024/m01); worker's wage or provision (quranic:root_001046:B004/m01).
- Ayah anchors: 27:15,19,43,45,59,91 `ع ب د` (عِبَادِ/تَعْبُدُ/اعْبُدُوا/أَعْبُدَ); 27:1,28-29,40,75 `ك ت ب` (كِتَابٍ/كِتَابِي/كِتَابٌ); 27:32 `ق ط ع` (قَاطِعَةً); 27:4,19,24,84,90,93 `ع م ل` (أَعْمَالَهُمْ/أَعْمَلَ/تَعْمَلُون); the primary surrender and worship anchors are 27:44 and 27:91.
- Synthesis: This legal scene usefully pressures the surah's language of authority and submission. A human contract converts compelled labor into freedom through payment to an owner, whereas the Queen submits with Solomon to God in 27:44 and Solomon names himself commanded to worship God in 27:91; her surrender is therefore not transfer into Solomon's ownership.
